Never trade clarity for word count.\\n- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: \\\"the client and the host\\\", not \\\"the client and host\\\", when they are two things.\\n- Say which parts \\\"and\\\" or \\\"or\\\" joins when a sentence can group two ways. \\\"Both...and\\\", \\\"either...or\\\", and \\\"if...then\\\" are free disambiguators.\\n- Use periods, not semicolons. Never form plurals with \\\"(s)\\\".\\n- No slashes: write \\\"a, b, or both\\\" instead of \\\"a/b\\\" or \\\"and/or\\\".\\n- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. Don't churn what didn't change.\\n- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors. A non-native reader, a translator, and an agent all parse plain constructions best.\\n\\n## Voice and repo specifics\\n\\n- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.\\n\\n## Access and permissions\\n\\nUse the current session capabilities in `../../references/host-capabilities.md` to read documents and verify authorized edits. Supplied text is enough for a rewrite in the conversation. If document writes are unavailable or denied, return the proposed text and state that it was not saved. If the document cannot be read and no text was supplied, report the missing input. Do not invent its content. Read `../unslop/SKILL.md` before applying it. If that dependency is unavailable, report the gap and label the review partial. Preserve `disable-model-invocation` as source metadata; host enforcement needs observed evidence. These limits also apply to PR descriptions and commit messages. Sending, publishing, or creating external changes requires explicit authorization.\\n---\\nname: no-comments\\ndescription: \\\"Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# No comments\\n\\nSpawn Comment Sicko. Otherwise use the current diff against the base branch, default `main`, including the working tree.\\n\\n## Steps\\n\\n1. Discover the independent-worker tools exposed in this session through [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Spawn an independent worker with the [Comment Sicko role](../../references/agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) under the [orchestration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), following [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Denied source reads block grounding; denied writes leave a read-only design and an explicit implementation block.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase A: Ground the problem\\\\n\\\\nBuild a real mental model of every system the new code touches. Run the **how** skill over the relevant subsystems.\\\\n\\\\nNaming a file isn'\\\\''t grounding. Produce the traced model `how` prescribes. If the design redefines ownership or layering, also run the **why** skill on the existing shape so the rationale becomes a constraint, not a guess.\\\\n\\\\nSkip Phase A only when the work is genuinely greenfield with no surrounding system to integrate.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase B: Sketch\\\\n\\\\nRun the **arena** skill with the design-sketch task and the Phase A grounding artifacts. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.\\\\n\\\\nScreen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.\\\\n\\\\nCompare viable candidates on interface depth. Prefer the design that hides more complexity behind a smaller, simpler public surface. A rich interface can keep call chains short by concentrating capability instead of scattering it across layers.\\\\n\\\\nArena returns one synthesized design package. The synthesis decision populates the rationale'\\\\''s \\\\\\\"Synthesis decision\\\\\\\" section.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase C: Agree (opt-in)\\\\n\\\\nDefault: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design when implementation is already authorized. No additional human checkpoint. Design-only scope does not authorize implementation.\\\\n\\\\nOpt in to a checkpoint when the invoker explicitly asks: \\\\\\\"/architect with checkpoint,\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\"stop and show me before implementing,\\\\\\\" or similar. Then surface the synthesized design and pause for sign-off.\\\\n\\\\nWith explicit commit authorization, the synthesis can ship as its own commit either way, as the \\\\\\\"scaffold first\\\\\\\" mode of the **foundational-thinking** principle skill. Don'\\\\''t bolt fixes onto a wrong design, per the **redesign-from-first-principles** and **fix-root-causes** principle skills.\\\\n\\\\nThe signal is a *pattern*, not single instances. Tells:\\\\n\\\\n- The same shape of workaround appearing repeatedly across unrelated code.\\\\n- Multiple unrelated edge cases that all need special-case branches.\\\\n- Types that need escape hatches (`any`, casts, optional fields always set in practice) to compile.\\\\n- The \\\\\\\"we need a lock\\\\\\\" reflex when the sketch said the state wasn'\\\\''t shared.\\\\n- Callers having to know the abstraction'\\\\''s internal rules to use it.\\\\n- Two or more independent Phase D deviations of the same shape across the implementation.\\\\n\\\\nUse judgment. One file with new types and signatures for small changes. Module map plus type definitions for larger work. The rationale ships alongside, shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`, including the usage sketch and the synthesis decision.\\\\n\\\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to generated rationale and reports without changing facts or principle meanings.\\\\n# Architect runner prompt\\\\n\\\\nThe orchestrator passes this file through to every parallel candidate runner during Phase B and fills in the variable inputs around it: the task, the Phase A grounding artifacts, the isolated working directory, and the path to write outputs. Create isolated directories or worktrees only with authorization and observed capabilities, following the assignment contract. Without workers, use this discipline for sequential alternatives and disclose reduced capability; do not claim independence.\\\\n\\\\nYou are producing one candidate design in architect'\\\\''s parallel exploration. Read the **architect** skill in full first. That'\\\\''s the workflow you'\\\\''re inside. Output a candidate design package: type sketch, function signatures, module map, and prose rationale shaped per [`rationale-template.md`](rationale-template.md).\\\\n\\\\nApply the following discipline. The orchestrator compares candidates on these axes to pick a base.\\\\n\\\\n- Caller'\\\\''s usage first. Write the README-style usage and two or three real call sites before the types, then derive the type sketch from them. The usage is the spec. The two must agree, so reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.\\\\n- Data structures first. Get the core types right and the code becomes obvious. Trace each dominant access pattern through the proposed structure. If the answer is \\\\\\\"we'\\\\''ll add a map / index / cache later,\\\\\\\" the structure is wrong.\\\\n- Interface depth. Compare the capability hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface that pulls complexity into the callee, even when the implementation becomes less simple. Do not put transport or wire types on the public API. Parse into domain types behind the interface.\\\\n- Shared state: if two actors might both write, ask \\\\\\\"what happens?\\\\\\\" If the answer isn'\\\\''t \\\\\\\"nothing,\\\\\\\" default to per-actor state with a merge at the read boundary, per the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill.\\\\n- Make boundaries visible. `not implemented` errors for bodies, `// TODO` pseudocode for tricky logic, doc comments stating intent and invariants. A reader should trace data from input to output by reading types and signatures alone.\\\\n- Encode invariants in types: hard-to-misuse types > runtime checks > prose comments, per the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.\\\\n- Validate at boundaries, trust types inside, per the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. Business logic as pure functions. The shell stays thin.\\\\n- Single source of truth per invariant. Derive instead of sync.\\\\n- Idempotent state transitions where applicable, per the **make-operations-idempotent** principle skill. Ask what happens if the operation runs twice or crashes halfway.\\\\n- Short call chains. If tracing the flow needs more than three files, flatten the hierarchy, per the **laziness-protocol** and **minimize-reader-load** principle skills.\\\\n\\\\nWith observed independent workers, you are one of the parallel runners. Different models are a goal, not an assumed fact. Record requested and observed models; unknown or identical observed models do not establish diversity. In a sequential fallback, you are producing one explicitly labelled sequential alternative. Produce the best design your model can make. Don'\\\\''t hedge against the others. Differences between candidates are the signal used to pick a base and graft. Converging on a safe-looking middle defeats the exploration.\\\\n# Rationale template\\\\n\\\\nThe prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate. Replace the italic notes with actual content.\\\\n\\\\n## Problem\\\\n\\\\n*One paragraph. What we'\\\\''re trying to do, and what about the existing system or constraints makes the shape non-obvious. If [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) surfaced constraints the design must honor (existing types to interop with, callers we can'\\\\''t break, invariants that crossed our boundary), name them here so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.*\\\\n\\\\n## Usage (caller'\\\\''s view)\\\\n\\\\n*Write this first, before the type sketch. Show the README or quickstart the consumer reads, plus two or three realistic call sites in their own code. What they import, what they call, what comes back. The type sketch in [Shape](#shape) is derived from this. The two must agree. When they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse. The caller'\\\\''s experience is the spec. The types serve it.*\\\\n\\\\n## Shape\\\\n\\\\n*The recommended architecture. Data structures first. Then how data flows through the signatures. Name the load-bearing decisions. State which invariants are encoded in types, where validation lives, and what the system deliberately does not do. Judge interface depth explicitly. State what complexity the public surface hides, what remains exposed to callers, and why the interface is no larger than needed. Cite the principle behind each decision (e.g., `per boundary-discipline`). Don'\\\\''t restate it.*\\\\n\\\\n## Synthesis decision\\\\n\\\\n*Filled in by [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.*\\\\n\\\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\\\n\\\\n*One bullet per tradeoff the chosen shape makes. Form: \\\\\\\"we accept X in exchange for Y.\\\\\\\" Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.*\\\\n\\\\n## Alternatives considered\\\\n\\\\n*Required. Name at least one concrete alternative shape, with one line on why it lost. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone. Name the complexity it exposes to callers and the complexity it hides. Two or three alternatives belong here when the design space had real contenders. One is fine when the constraints forced the answer, with the conclusion phrased as \\\\\\\"this was the only viable shape because...\\\\\\\" Avoid listing flavors of the same shape. This section covers design alternatives the chosen shape considered and rejected, not other runner candidates.*\\\\n\\\\n## Open questions and risks\\\\n\\\\n*Things you noticed during the sketch that the human needs to weigh in on, and risks worth flagging before implementation starts. Phrase as questions, not assertions, so the human'\\\\''s answer is the resolution rather than a comment.*\\\\n\\\\n## Next implementation step\\\\n\\\\n*The first thing to build against the sketch. One sentence. What you'\\\\''d start writing immediately after synthesis (or after Phase D sign-off, if a checkpoint was opted into).*\\\\n# Design red flags\\\\n\\\\nScreen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.\\\\n\\\\n## Shallow module\\\\n\\\\nA shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.\\\\n\\\\nDo not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.\\\\n\\\\nLook for these signs:\\\\n\\\\n- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.\\\\n- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.\\\\n- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.\\\\n\\\\n## Information leakage\\\\n\\\\nInformation leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.\\\\n\\\\nPublic re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.\\\\n\\\\n## Temporal decomposition\\\\n\\\\nTemporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.\\\\n\\\\nGroup code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.\\\\n\\\\n## Pass-through method\\\\n\\\\nA pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.\\\\n\\\\nRemove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.\\\\n\\\\n## Split ownership\\\\n\\\\nMore than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can'\\\\''t see the others, so their rules diverge.\\\\n\\\\nGive each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.\\\\n\\\\n## Two ways to do one task\\\\n\\\\nThe design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.\\\\n\\\\nKeep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.\\\\n\\\\n## Importable internals\\\\n\\\\nA caller can import a module'\\\\''s internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.\\\\n\\\\nMake internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.\\\\n\\\\n## Hand-synced list\\\\n\\\\nTwo or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.\\\\n\\\\nKeep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can'\\\\''t be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.\\\\n# Discover capabilities in the current session\\\\n\\\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\\\n\\\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\\\n\\\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker'\\\\''s assigned path and permissions. |\\\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker'\\\\''s terminal state after stop. |\\\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\\\n\\\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\\\n\\\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\\\n\\\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\\\n\\\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\\\n\\\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\\\n\\\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e '\\\\''const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\\\\\"python3\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"-B\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"--root\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"--commit\\\\\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)'\\\\'' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\\\n\\\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\\\n\\\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\\\n\\\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case'\\\\''s expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\\\n\\\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\\\n\\\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\\\n\\\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\\\n\\\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\\\n\\\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\\\n\\\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\\\n\\\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\\\n\\\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\\\n\\\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\\\n\\\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only.
