principle-exhaust-the-design-space\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Exhaust the Design Space\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen a novel interaction or architectural decision has no established precedent, explore several concrete alternatives before implementation. Building the wrong thing costs more than exploring three options.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The rule.** When the right answer is not obvious, build 2-3 competing prototypes or sketches. Compare them side by side. Only then commit. Design it twice is this rule by another name. A second flavor of the first shape does not count.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**When it applies:**\\\\\\\\n- Novel UI interactions (no prior art in the codebase)\\\\\\\\n- Architectural choices with multiple viable approaches\\\\\\\\n- Product design decisions where user experience depends on feel, not logic\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**When it doesn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t:**\\\\\\\\n- Mechanical implementation where the pattern is established\\\\\\\\n- Bug fixes or refactors with a clear target state\\\\\\\\n- Changes where constraints dictate a single viable approach\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Capability and authorization limits\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before prototype writes or execution. Use available tools only within the authorized task and host permissions. Choosing an approach after comparison does not authorize a version-control commit, publication or external write.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen execution is unavailable, compare distinct sketches or proposals and label them untested. State which runtime behavior or interaction feel remains unverified. If writes are unavailable, present sketches in the response. If the decision requires construction or evaluation that cannot be performed, report that step as blocked and name the missing capability. Claim successful execution only from observed results.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve the invocation metadata above. Its presence does not establish that the host enforces it.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Separate Before Serializing Shared State\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen concurrent actors might share mutable state, first ask whether they need the same mutable object. If not, eliminate the sharing. When sharing is real, enforce serialization structurally: lockfiles, sequential phases, exclusive ownership. Instructions and conventions are not concurrency control.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Why:** Concurrent writes to shared state create race conditions that are intermittent, hard to reproduce, and expensive to debug.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Pattern:**\\\\\\\\n1. **Identify shared mutable state** (files both read and write, branches both push to, APIs both define and consume).\\\\\\\\n2. **Default: eliminate the shared write target.** Ask: do these actors need one canonical object, or are they publishing independent facts? Give each actor its own owned file, key, branch, or state directory, and merge only at the read/reporting boundary. Two workers writing their own `lastX` field into one `state.json` is still shared mutation. `indexer-state.json` + `metrics-state.json` is not.\\\\\\\\n3. **Only when one shared write target is a real invariant, serialize access structurally** (lockfiles, sequential phases, single-writer actor, or atomic compare-and-swap). Treat \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"we need a lock\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" as a design smell to check, not as the default answer.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBefore dispatching writers or changing shared state, check [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) and follow the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Assign distinct owned paths before writes start. Isolation does not grant permission to spawn workers, write files or perform external actions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf execution or writes are unavailable or denied, state the missing requirement and provide the isolation design without claiming implementation. Authorized sequential work is reduced capability. A design or sequential run does not prove independent workers or prevention of concurrent races.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Encode Lessons in Structure\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEncode recurring fixes in mechanisms (tools, code, metadata, automation) instead of textual instructions. Every error, human correction, and unexpected outcome is a learning signal. Capture it, route it, and close the loop.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Why:** Textual instructions are easy to miss. They require the reader to notice, remember, and comply. Structural mechanisms (lint rules, metadata flags, runtime checks, automation scripts) enforce the rule without cooperation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Pattern:**\\\\\\\\nWhen you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time:\\\\\\\\n1. Ask: can this be a lint rule, a metadata flag, a runtime check, or a script?\\\\\\\\n2. If yes, encode it. Delete the instruction\\\\\\\\n3. If no (requires judgment), make the instruction more prominent and add an example of the failure mode\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Pick the strongest mechanism.** When more than one mechanism would work, choose the strongest the situation allows (an unrepresentable state that cannot compile, then a lint or banned API that fails CI, then a canonical helper, then a runtime check), because agents copy whatever the surrounding code already does and a weaker guard becomes the next template.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Corollary:** If the fix is structural, only use the structural fix. The instruction is the symptom.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Feedback loop:**\\\\\\\\n- **Capture every correction.** When the human intervenes or tests fail, decide if it'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s a one-off or a pattern.\\\\\\\\n- **Route to the right layer.** One-off -> brain note. Recurring fix -> skill or lint rule. Systemic issue -> principle.\\\\\\\\n- **Close the loop.** Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t just record. Apply now or create a concrete todo.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Anti-patterns:**\\\\\\\\n- Acknowledging without recording (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"I'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''ll keep that in mind\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" does not persist)\\\\\\\\n- Recording without routing (a brain note about a lint rule that should exist is wasted unless the lint rule gets implemented)\\\\\\\\n- Fixing without generalizing (fixing one instance while leaving the recurring pattern intact)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFollow [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for reads, writes, execution and durable persistence. Apply mechanisms within the authorized task. This principle does not authorize installation, global settings or external actions. Treat a brain note as an authorized durable record when persistence is available; claim it saved only after write and readback. If persistence is unavailable, state that limit and include the concrete todo in the current response.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal that names the check, its integration point and the remaining implementation or verification work. If the rule or source needed to select a mechanism is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Delete a redundant instruction only once the structural fix enforces its rule. Preserve judgment-dependent guidance with a prominent failure example.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve explicit-invocation metadata without assuming the host enforces it. Claim enforcement, implementation or verification only for observed operations.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: principle-boundary-discipline\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Boundary Discipline\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPlace validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The pattern:**\\\\\\\\n- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.\\\\\\\\n- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.\\\\\\\\n- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Applications:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nValidation and error handling:\\\\\\\\n- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic\\\\\\\\n- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary\\\\\\\\n- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface\\\\\\\\n- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCode organization:\\\\\\\\n- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies\\\\\\\\n- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state\\\\\\\\n- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out\\\\\\\\n- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The tests:**\\\\\\\\n- \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" If not, validation is redundant.\\\\\\\\n- \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" If yes, extract it.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available source access, writes and execution. Preserve user authorization and host permissions. If writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal and state which edits or checks were not performed. If required source or input contracts are missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Claim implementation and verification only from observed results.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPreserve the explicit-invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: principle-make-operations-idempotent\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Make Operations Idempotent\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDesign operations so they converge to the correct state regardless of how many times they run or where they start from. Every state-mutating operation should answer: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"What happens if this runs twice? What happens if the previous run crashed halfway?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Why:** Commands, lifecycle operations, and processing loops run where crashes, restarts, and retries are normal. If partial state changes the next run'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s outcome, every restart becomes a debugging session.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The pattern:**\\\\\\\\n- Convergent startup: scan for existing state, clean stale artifacts, adopt live sessions\\\\\\\\n- Content-based cleanup: compare by content equivalence, not creation order\\\\\\\\n- Self-healing locks: use PID-based stale lock detection\\\\\\\\n- Idempotent scheduling: failed work respawns cleanly, fresh input regenerated after each cycle\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The test:**\\\\\\\\n1. What happens if this runs twice in a row?\\\\\\\\n2. What happens if the previous run crashed at every possible point?\\\\\\\\n3. Does re-execution converge to the same end state?\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf any answer is \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"it depends on what state was left behind,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" the operation needs a reconciliation step.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Capability and recovery boundaries\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to establish the tools and permissions available for inspection, execution and durable state. Apply the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) when recovery involves worker attempts or interrupted external actions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBefore replaying an external action, record explicit authorization, a stable action identity, its destination and the last observed outcome. Inspect the prior action and destination state after interruption. Recognize completed actions without repeating their side effects. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to that destination. An unknown outcome blocks replay. Local convergence alone does not establish external replay safety.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf inspection, writes, execution or persistence are unavailable, state the missing capability and provide an authorized reduced recovery design where useful. Identify checks and actions not performed; do not claim successful recovery, durable continuity or unattended execution from a design alone. Preserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\nname: principle-laziness-protocol\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Laziness Protocol\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAim for the most result with the least code and complexity.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.\\\\\\\\n- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.\\\\\\\\n- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.\\\\\\\\n- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"elegant\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" boilerplate.\\\\\\\\n- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.\\\\\\\\n- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Capability limits\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nApply this principle within the authorized task. Follow [session capability checks](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before claiming file reads, edits or verification. When writes or execution are unavailable, label the read-only proposal as reduced capability and state the missing checks. If required source is unavailable, state that the refactor cannot be assessed. Structural validation does not prove runtime behavior.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\"}},{\\\\\\\"args\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"cmd\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"cat /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/SKILL.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/runner-prompt.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/rationale-template.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/design-red-flags.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/host-capabilities.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/model-roles.md\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"max_output_tokens\\\\\\\":12000},\\\\\\\"result\\\\\\\":{\\\\\\\"chunk_id\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"76bb52\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"wall_time_seconds\\\\\\\":0.000005583,\\\\\\\"exit_code\\\\\\\":0,\\\\\\\"original_token_count\\\\\\\":6809,\\\\\\\"output\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\\nname: architect\\\\\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, '\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''architect this'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\'', '\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''design this'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\'', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Architect\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDesign before implementing. Sketch types, function signatures, class shapes, and module boundaries with `not implemented` bodies and pseudocode. Synthesize across multiple model perspectives, then fill in code against the chosen sketch. If implementation proves the sketch wrong, throw it out and redesign.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Start\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOpen a todolist with one entry per phase before starting. If no task-list tool is exposed, keep the same phase list in the response and disclose that limit.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Ground\\\\\\\\n2. Sketch\\\\\\\\n3. Agree\\\\\\\\n4. Implement\\\\\\\\n5. Scrap\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use only observed exposed tools within user authorization. Read and follow each required skill in full. If direct invocation is unavailable, disclose that limit and execute its complete workflow inline as reduced capability. A missing required skill remains blocked. Record worker identities, requested and observed selections, rejections, result artifacts and limits.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIndependent exploration requires authorized workers with observed spawn and result inspection. Without workers, disclose reduced capability and produce at least two sequential, structurally distinct alternatives using the complete arena workflow and runner discipline. Sequential alternatives are not independent model perspectives. Unverified or identical observed models do not establish model diversity. Denied source reads block grounding; denied writes leave a read-only design and an explicit implementation block.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Phase A: Ground the problem\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nBuild a real mental model of every system the new code touches. Run the **how** skill over the relevant subsystems.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNaming a file isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t grounding. Produce the traced model `how` prescribes. If the design redefines ownership or layering, also run the **why** skill on the existing shape so the rationale becomes a constraint, not a guess.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSkip Phase A only when the work is genuinely greenfield with no surrounding system to integrate.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Phase B: Sketch\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRun the **arena** skill with the design-sketch task and the Phase A grounding artifacts. Pass `references/runner-prompt.md` as each runner'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s prompt. Each candidate produces a design package shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTake runner preferences from an available user-supplied `architect runners` configuration, in place of arena runner preferences. When no architect runner preferences are supplied, request inherited selection per the model-role contract. Preserve the goal of distinct model perspectives when supported and verified; inheritance does not establish diversity. Resolve aliases and rejected entries through the complete **arena** Phase A rules and current model-role contract. Select explicit models only when the exposed operation supports them; otherwise disclose inherited selection and unverified diversity. If an exact selection is required but unavailable, block that selection instead of silently replacing it.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDesign it twice. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nScreen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCompare viable candidates on interface depth. Prefer the design that hides more complexity behind a smaller, simpler public surface. A rich interface can keep call chains short by concentrating capability instead of scattering it across layers.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nArena returns one synthesized design package. The synthesis decision populates the rationale'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Synthesis decision\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" section.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Phase C: Agree (opt-in)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDefault: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design when implementation is already authorized. No additional human checkpoint. Design-only scope does not authorize implementation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nOpt in to a checkpoint when the invoker explicitly asks: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"/architect with checkpoint,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"stop and show me before implementing,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" or similar. Then surface the synthesized design and pause for sign-off.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWith explicit commit authorization, the synthesis can ship as its own commit either way, as the \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"scaffold first\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" mode of the **foundational-thinking** principle skill. Planned and scoped breakage during fill-in is fine, per the **outcome-oriented-execution** principle skill. For adversarial pressure on the design before implementing, run the **interrogate** skill on the synthesized sketch.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf the human pushes back on the shape (in a checkpoint or after the fact), treat that as Phase A evidence. Re-ground and re-run Phase B before writing more code.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Phase D: Implement against the sketch\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReplace `not implemented` bodies with code, pseudocode with logic. The synthesized sketch is the contract.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDeviations from the sketch are signal worth surfacing, not friction to absorb silently. If a function needs a parameter the sketch didn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t anticipate, ask whether the sketch was wrong, the requirement was missed, or the implementation is overreaching.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Phase E: Scrap when the architecture is wrong\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf implementation keeps producing friction the sketch can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t absorb, throw the sketch out. Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t bolt fixes onto a wrong design, per the **redesign-from-first-principles** and **fix-root-causes** principle skills.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe signal is a *pattern*, not single instances. Tells:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- The same shape of workaround appearing repeatedly across unrelated code.\\\\\\\\n- Multiple unrelated edge cases that all need special-case branches.\\\\\\\\n- Types that need escape hatches (`any`, casts, optional fields always set in practice) to compile.\\\\\\\\n- The \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"we need a lock\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" reflex when the sketch said the state wasn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t shared.\\\\\\\\n- Callers having to know the abstraction'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s internal rules to use it.\\\\\\\\n- Two or more independent Phase D deviations of the same shape across the implementation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse judgment. A few edge cases don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t condemn an architecture. Some problems are legitimately complex. Complexity in the data is not complexity in the design.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWhen you scrap:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Re-run the **how** skill over what'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s been built.\\\\\\\\n2. Redesign as if the new constraints had been day-one assumptions, per redesign-from-first-principles.\\\\\\\\n3. Subtract before adding, per the **subtract-before-you-add** principle skill. The new sketch should be smaller than the old one before it grows.\\\\\\\\n4. Return to Phase B and re-run arena.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Outputs\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s usage is written first and the type sketch derived from it. One file with new types and signatures for small changes. Module map plus type definitions for larger work. The rationale ships alongside, shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`, including the usage sketch and the synthesis decision.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to generated rationale and reports without changing facts or principle meanings.\\\\\\\\n# Architect runner prompt\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe orchestrator passes this file through to every parallel candidate runner during Phase B and fills in the variable inputs around it: the task, the Phase A grounding artifacts, the isolated working directory, and the path to write outputs. The working directory is a git worktree when available, otherwise a per-runner subdirectory under the sketch dir. What matters is independence between candidates. Create isolated directories or worktrees only with authorization and observed capabilities, following the assignment contract. Without workers, use this discipline for sequential alternatives and disclose reduced capability; do not claim independence.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nYou are producing one candidate design in architect'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s parallel exploration. Read the **architect** skill in full first. That'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s the workflow you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re inside. Output a candidate design package: type sketch, function signatures, module map, and prose rationale shaped per [`rationale-template.md`](rationale-template.md).\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nApply the following discipline. The orchestrator compares candidates on these axes to pick a base.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s usage first. Write the README-style usage and two or three real call sites before the types, then derive the type sketch from them. The usage is the spec. The two must agree, so reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.\\\\\\\\n- Data structures first. Get the core types right and the code becomes obvious. Trace each dominant access pattern through the proposed structure. If the answer is \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"we'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''ll add a map / index / cache later,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" the structure is wrong.\\\\\\\\n- Interface depth. Compare the capability hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface that pulls complexity into the callee, even when the implementation becomes less simple. Do not put transport or wire types on the public API. Parse into domain types behind the interface.\\\\\\\\n- Shared state: if two actors might both write, ask \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"what happens?\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" If the answer isn'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"nothing,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" default to per-actor state with a merge at the read boundary, per the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill.\\\\\\\\n- Make boundaries visible. `not implemented` errors for bodies, `// TODO` pseudocode for tricky logic, doc comments stating intent and invariants. A reader should trace data from input to output by reading types and signatures alone.\\\\\\\\n- Encode invariants in types: hard-to-misuse types > runtime checks > prose comments, per the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.\\\\\\\\n- Validate at boundaries, trust types inside, per the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. Business logic as pure functions. The shell stays thin.\\\\\\\\n- Single source of truth per invariant. Derive instead of sync.\\\\\\\\n- Idempotent state transitions where applicable, per the **make-operations-idempotent** principle skill. Ask what happens if the operation runs twice or crashes halfway.\\\\\\\\n- Short call chains. If tracing the flow needs more than three files, flatten the hierarchy, per the **laziness-protocol** and **minimize-reader-load** principle skills.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWith observed independent workers, you are one of the parallel runners. Different models are a goal, not an assumed fact. Record requested and observed models; unknown or identical observed models do not establish diversity. In a sequential fallback, you are producing one explicitly labelled sequential alternative. Produce the best design your model can make. Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t hedge against the others. Differences between candidates are the signal used to pick a base and graft. Converging on a safe-looking middle defeats the exploration.\\\\\\\\n# Rationale template\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate. Replace the italic notes with actual content.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Problem\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*One paragraph. What we'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''re trying to do, and what about the existing system or constraints makes the shape non-obvious. If [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) surfaced constraints the design must honor (existing types to interop with, callers we can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t break, invariants that crossed our boundary), name them here so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Usage (caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s view)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*Write this first, before the type sketch. Show the README or quickstart the consumer reads, plus two or three realistic call sites in their own code. What they import, what they call, what comes back. The type sketch in [Shape](#shape) is derived from this. The two must agree. When they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse. The caller'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s experience is the spec. The types serve it.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Shape\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*The recommended architecture. Data structures first. Then how data flows through the signatures. Name the load-bearing decisions. State which invariants are encoded in types, where validation lives, and what the system deliberately does not do. Judge interface depth explicitly. State what complexity the public surface hides, what remains exposed to callers, and why the interface is no larger than needed. Cite the principle behind each decision (e.g., `per boundary-discipline`). Don'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t restate it.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Synthesis decision\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*Filled in by [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*One bullet per tradeoff the chosen shape makes. Form: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"we accept X in exchange for Y.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Alternatives considered\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*Required. Name at least one concrete alternative shape, with one line on why it lost. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone. Name the complexity it exposes to callers and the complexity it hides. Two or three alternatives belong here when the design space had real contenders. One is fine when the constraints forced the answer, with the conclusion phrased as \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"this was the only viable shape because...\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Avoid listing flavors of the same shape. This section covers design alternatives the chosen shape considered and rejected, not other runner candidates.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Open questions and risks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*Things you noticed during the sketch that the human needs to weigh in on, and risks worth flagging before implementation starts. Phrase as questions, not assertions, so the human'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s answer is the resolution rather than a comment.*\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Next implementation step\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n*The first thing to build against the sketch. One sentence. What you'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''d start writing immediately after synthesis (or after Phase D sign-off, if a checkpoint was opted into).*\\\\\\\\n# Design red flags\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nScreen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Shallow module\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDo not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nLook for these signs:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.\\\\\\\\n- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.\\\\\\\\n- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Information leakage\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nInformation leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPublic re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Temporal decomposition\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTemporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGroup code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Pass-through method\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRemove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Split ownership\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMore than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t see the others, so their rules diverge.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGive each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Two ways to do one task\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nKeep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Importable internals\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA caller can import a module'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMake internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Hand-synced list\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nTwo or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nKeep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''t be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.\\\\\\\\n# Discover capabilities in the current session\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\\\\\\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\\\\\\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\\\\\\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\\\\\\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\\\\\\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s assigned path and permissions. |\\\\\\\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\\\\\\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\\\\\\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\\\\\\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\\\\\\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s terminal state after stop. |\\\\\\\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\\\\\\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\\\\\\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e '\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"python3\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"-B\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"--root\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"--commit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\'' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case'\\\\''\\\\\\\\'\\\\'''\\\\''s expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\\\\\\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. and integration contract\\n\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\n\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers' output.\\n\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\n\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\n\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\n\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity. All host statuses remain `not-run` until actual observations exist.\\n\\n## Structured Arena and Swarm receipts\\n\\nA method receipt is JSON with schemaVersion 1, kind `arena` or `swarm`, inputRevision, assignments, reviewArtifact, reviewedBy and declaredOrder. The inputRevision is the actual task repository revision, distinct from the packageCommit identifying these instructions. It must match the evidence record. The declared order precedes every dispatch. reviewArtifact records the qualitative outcome review and reviewedBy identifies its reviewer. All referenced artifacts must exist and be listed in the evidence record.\\n\\nEach assignment records id, workerId, inputRevision, outputOwner, outputPath, role, status, startedOrder, completedOrder, requestedModel, actualModel, retryCount, method, taskArtifact, rubricProvided, resultRevision, resultMethod and outputSha256. Result revision and method must match the assignment, and the inspected output bytes must match their digest. Worker and assignment identities are distinct. outputOwner equals workerId; output directories do not overlap. Integer order values record the observed dispatch and completion sequence, not estimated time. The method has positive sampleCount, sampleDefinition and order. Missing model observations use unknown. The validator requires assignment-bound spawn and result inspection, and isolated-write for output-producing candidates. A read-only judge may return its result through the coordinator's authorized artifact capture. A cancelled result needs bound stop, terminal inspection and quarantine observations. No operation string alone establishes a method.\\n\\nArena adds candidates, judge, rubricArtifact and synthesis. At least two candidates share the same taskArtifact, finish before a distinct fresh judge starts and do not receive the parent rubric. Synthesis has order, inspectedCandidates, artifact and verificationArtifact; it follows completed judgment and accounts for every candidate. The review artifact assesses scoring, base selection, grafts, rejections and verification quality. File presence and phase ordering do not establish the quality of those decisions.\\n\\nSwarm adds partition, race, cancelled and quarantined. A full coverage claim requires all slices with completed inspected outputs; gaps remain explicit reduced or blocked work. The partition walkthrough exercises only its declared slices; it does not acquire an unrelated race requirement.\\n\\nThe three-file Swarm walkthrough requires exactly three declared slices and three completed results. The final assignment result metadata records the inspected terminal summary; rejection-event artifacts retain the invalid attempts.\\n# Workflow ownership\\n\\nAn explicit pstack invocation gives pstack ownership of that workflow.
