If there isn't, don't force one\\n- If the explorers flagged open questions or gaps, acknowledge them rather than hiding them\\n# Epistemics\\n\\nHow to reason about confidence when evidence is historical, fragmentary, and sometimes contradictory, and how to communicate it without flattening it into false certainty.\\n\\nCode doesn't carry its own motivation. You can read what code does. You can't read *why it exists*. That lives in commits, PRs, tickets, docs, and conversations, all incomplete, biased, and sometimes missing entirely. Pretending otherwise produces confident-sounding guesses that mislead the user.\\n\\n## Confidence Tiers\\n\\nEvery claim in the final output must sit in one of these tiers. The tier determines which output section the claim goes in and how it's phrased.\\n\\n### 1. Direct\\n\\nAn explicit, textual citation that answers the question. Not \\\"the code does X so the author must have wanted X.\\\" Something an author actually *wrote* that says why.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- A PR description that says \\\"this fixes the bug where users with >1000 items couldn't paginate\\\"\\n- A ticket that says \\\"we're adding this because customer Acme requested it in their security review\\\"\\n- A code comment that says \\\"// clamp to 100 because the upstream API rejects larger values\\\"\\n- A design doc that says \\\"we chose option A over option B because we need persistence across restarts\\\"\\n- A chat message from the author saying \\\"switching to this approach since the old one was flaky in tests\\\"\\n\\nPhrasing: confident, present tense. \\\"This exists because X.\\\" Cite the source.\\n\\n### 2. Supported\\n\\nMultiple pieces of indirect evidence converge. No single source states it explicitly, but the pattern across sources makes it likely.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- The PR title says \\\"improve performance,\\\" the ticket is labeled \\\"perf,\\\" and the surrounding commits all touch the same hot path\\n- Multiple tests were added alongside the change, all exercising edge cases with very large inputs\\n- The author's other PRs from the same week all mention the same incident in their descriptions\\n\\nPhrasing: confident but clearly derived. \\\"The evidence points strongly to X: [the specific pieces].\\\" Cite multiple sources.\\n\\n### 3. Inferred\\n\\nA reasonable reading of the context, but nothing explicitly supports it. The reader should understand this is *your interpretation*, not a fact from the record.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- The PR doesn't say why, but given the error was happening in production (per the incident channel timing) and the fix was rushed (merged the same day), it was likely a hotfix.\\n- The function name suggests retry logic. The retry count is 3. This matches the team's general convention of \\\"3 retries\\\" seen elsewhere in the codebase.\\n\\nPhrasing: hedged. \\\"It appears\\\", \\\"likely\\\", \\\"suggests\\\", \\\"is consistent with\\\", \\\"one reading is\\\". Make the inference chain explicit: \\\"Given A and B, C seems likely because D.\\\"\\n\\n### 4. Speculative\\n\\nA plausible hypothesis, but the evidence is thin and other explanations fit equally well. Presenting these is valuable, but mark them clearly as guesses.\\n\\nExamples:\\n- \\\"This might be a workaround for a browser bug that's since been fixed, but we found no contemporary evidence of that.\\\"\\n- \\\"It's possible this threshold was chosen to match an SLA commitment, but no SLA doc references it.\\\"\\n\\nPhrasing: explicitly speculative. \\\"One possibility is X, but we have no direct evidence.\\\" Usually lives in the \\\"Competing Hypotheses\\\" section alongside other possibilities.\\n\\n### 5. Unknown\\n\\nYou looked and couldn't find out. A valid and important outcome. Document it.\\n\\nPhrasing: \\\"We searched X, Y, and Z and found no evidence of why.\\\" Be specific about *what* you searched. \\\"We couldn't find out\\\" is less useful than \\\"we searched the ticket tracker with keywords A and B, scanned the 6 PRs that touched this file since 2023, and grep'd the repo for string literals matching the threshold. None surfaced a rationale.\\\"\\n\\n## Phrasing Guide\\n\\n### Words that carry confidence. Use carefully\\n\\nThese imply **Direct** or **Supported** confidence. Don't use them for inferences.\\n\\n- \\\"because\\\". Implies a causal claim with evidence\\n- \\\"the reason is\\\". Same\\n- \\\"was designed to\\\". Claims author intent\\n- \\\"fixes\\\", \\\"addresses\\\", \\\"solves\\\". Claims the change achieved its goal\\n- \\\"the team decided\\\". Claims a group decision happened\\n\\nIf you're using these, you should have a citation immediately adjacent.\\n\\n### Words that hedge. Use for inferences\\n\\n- \\\"appears to\\\"\\n- \\\"seems to\\\"\\n- \\\"likely\\\"\\n- \\\"suggests\\\"\\n- \\\"is consistent with\\\"\\n- \\\"one reading is\\\"\\n- \\\"plausibly\\\"\\n- \\\"may have been\\\"\\n- \\\"the evidence points toward\\\"\\n\\nThese signal that you're interpreting, not reporting. Use them liberally in the \\\"What We Can Reasonably Infer\\\" section.\\n\\n### Words to avoid\\n\\n- \\\"obviously\\\". If it were obvious, the user wouldn't be asking\\n- \\\"clearly\\\". Almost always precedes a claim that isn't clear\\n- \\\"of course\\\". Same\\n- \\\"just\\\" (as in \\\"it's just X for performance\\\"). Dismissive and usually hides uncertainty\\n- \\\"I think\\\" / \\\"I believe\\\". You're synthesizing evidence, not giving a personal opinion. Use \\\"the evidence suggests\\\" instead.\\n\\n### Avoid rationalization\\n\\nCode that \\\"makes sense\\\" today may have been written for reasons that no longer apply, or that were wrong when they were written. Don't retrofit a clean rationale onto messy history.\\n\\nResist the urge to:\\n- Assume the author did the \\\"right\\\" thing and work backward to justify it\\n- Assume a consistent pattern across the codebase was intentional when it might be copy-paste\\n- Turn an absence of evidence into evidence of absence (\\\"no one mentioned security concerns, so it must not have been a concern\\\")\\n\\n## The Sycophancy Trap\\n\\nUsers often phrase `why` questions with an embedded hypothesis: \\\"Why do we do it this way, I assume it's for performance?\\\" Don't simply confirm it. Treat it as one candidate among others and check the evidence independently. If the evidence supports it, say so with citations. If not, say so and present what the evidence *does* support.\\n\\nThe user's guess is a prompt for investigation, not a conclusion to validate.\\n\\n## When Evidence Contradicts\\n\\nIf two sources disagree (the PR description says one thing, the ticket says another), surface both. Don't pick the one that fits a tidier narrative. A typical pattern:\\n\\n- **The ticket says** \\\"we need this for customer X's compliance requirement\\\"\\n- **The PR says** \\\"cleaning up tech debt in this area\\\"\\n\\nBoth may be true (the ticket motivated the work, the PR is the author's framing of it), or one may be wrong. Present both with their citations and let the user make the call.\\n\\n## When Evidence Is Missing\\n\\nAn honest \\\"we don't know\\\" is one of the most valuable outputs this skill can produce. The user now knows:\\n\\n- The answer isn't in the obvious places\\n- They'll need to ask a human (the original author, the product owner, the team lead) to find out\\n- Or they can decide the question isn't worth pursuing further\\n\\nFailing to mark a gap and filling it with a confident guess actively harms the user. They'll act on the guess.\\n\\nWhen you hit a gap, name it concretely:\\n- What question you were trying to answer\\n- What sources you searched\\n- What you searched for in each\\n- What you found (nothing, or only tangentially related material)\\n\\n## Calibration Check Before Finalizing\\n\\nBefore delivering the output, the synthesizer should review every claim in \\\"What We Found\\\" and \\\"What We Can Reasonably Infer\\\" and ask:\\n\\n1. Does this claim have a citation? If not, either add one or move it to \\\"Inferred\\\" / \\\"Hypotheses\\\".\\n2. Is the phrasing calibrated to the tier? (A Direct claim can use \\\"because\\\". An Inferred claim cannot.)\\n3. Am I treating the code itself as evidence for its own intent? If so, that's not evidence. Remove or reclassify.\\n4. Does the output include a \\\"What We Don't Know\\\" section? If no gaps are mentioned, that's suspicious. Either the evidence was unusually complete or something is being swept under the rug.\\n---\\nname: principle-exhaust-the-design-space\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Exhaust the Design Space\\n\\nWhen a novel interaction or architectural decision has no established precedent, explore several concrete alternatives before implementation. Building the wrong thing costs more than exploring three options.\\n\\n**The rule.** When the right answer is not obvious, build 2-3 competing prototypes or sketches. Compare them side by side. Only then commit. Design it twice is this rule by another name. A second flavor of the first shape does not count.\\n\\n**When it applies:**\\n- Novel UI interactions (no prior art in the codebase)\\n- Architectural choices with multiple viable approaches\\n- Product design decisions where user experience depends on feel, not logic\\n\\n**When it doesn't:**\\n- Mechanical implementation where the pattern is established\\n- Bug fixes or refactors with a clear target state\\n- Changes where constraints dictate a single viable approach\\n\\n## Capability and authorization limits\\n\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before prototype writes or execution. Use available tools only within the authorized task and host permissions. Choosing an approach after comparison does not authorize a version-control commit, publication or external write.\\n\\nWhen execution is unavailable, compare distinct sketches or proposals and label them untested. State which runtime behavior or interaction feel remains unverified. If writes are unavailable, present sketches in the response. If the decision requires construction or evaluation that cannot be performed, report that step as blocked and name the missing capability. Claim successful execution only from observed results.\\n\\nPreserve the invocation metadata above. Its presence does not establish that the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Separate Before Serializing Shared State\\n\\nWhen concurrent actors might share mutable state, first ask whether they need the same mutable object. If not, eliminate the sharing. When sharing is real, enforce serialization structurally: lockfiles, sequential phases, exclusive ownership. Instructions and conventions are not concurrency control.\\n\\n**Why:** Concurrent writes to shared state create race conditions that are intermittent, hard to reproduce, and expensive to debug.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\n1. **Identify shared mutable state** (files both read and write, branches both push to, APIs both define and consume).\\n2. **Default: eliminate the shared write target.** Ask: do these actors need one canonical object, or are they publishing independent facts? Give each actor its own owned file, key, branch, or state directory, and merge only at the read/reporting boundary. Two workers writing their own `lastX` field into one `state.json` is still shared mutation. `indexer-state.json` + `metrics-state.json` is not.\\n3. **Only when one shared write target is a real invariant, serialize access structurally** (lockfiles, sequential phases, single-writer actor, or atomic compare-and-swap). Treat \\\"we need a lock\\\" as a design smell to check, not as the default answer.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nBefore dispatching writers or changing shared state, check [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) and follow the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Assign distinct owned paths before writes start. Isolation does not grant permission to spawn workers, write files or perform external actions.\\n\\nIf execution or writes are unavailable or denied, state the missing requirement and provide the isolation design without claiming implementation. Authorized sequential work is reduced capability. A design or sequential run does not prove independent workers or prevention of concurrent races.\\n---\\nname: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Encode Lessons in Structure\\n\\nEncode recurring fixes in mechanisms (tools, code, metadata, automation) instead of textual instructions. Every error, human correction, and unexpected outcome is a learning signal. Capture it, route it, and close the loop.\\n\\n**Why:** Textual instructions are easy to miss. They require the reader to notice, remember, and comply. Structural mechanisms (lint rules, metadata flags, runtime checks, automation scripts) enforce the rule without cooperation.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\nWhen you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time:\\n1. Ask: can this be a lint rule, a metadata flag, a runtime check, or a script?\\n2. If yes, encode it. Delete the instruction\\n3. If no (requires judgment), make the instruction more prominent and add an example of the failure mode\\n\\n**Pick the strongest mechanism.** When more than one mechanism would work, choose the strongest the situation allows (an unrepresentable state that cannot compile, then a lint or banned API that fails CI, then a canonical helper, then a runtime check), because agents copy whatever the surrounding code already does and a weaker guard becomes the next template.\\n\\n**Corollary:** If the fix is structural, only use the structural fix. The instruction is the symptom.\\n\\n**Feedback loop:**\\n- **Capture every correction.** When the human intervenes or tests fail, decide if it's a one-off or a pattern.\\n- **Route to the right layer.** One-off -> brain note. Recurring fix -> skill or lint rule. Systemic issue -> principle.\\n- **Close the loop.** Don't just record. Apply now or create a concrete todo.\\n\\n**Anti-patterns:**\\n- Acknowledging without recording (\\\"I'll keep that in mind\\\" does not persist)\\n- Recording without routing (a brain note about a lint rule that should exist is wasted unless the lint rule gets implemented)\\n- Fixing without generalizing (fixing one instance while leaving the recurring pattern intact)\\n\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\n\\nFollow [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) for reads, writes, execution and durable persistence. Apply mechanisms within the authorized task. This principle does not authorize installation, global settings or external actions. Treat a brain note as an authorized durable record when persistence is available; claim it saved only after write and readback. If persistence is unavailable, state that limit and include the concrete todo in the current response.\\n\\nIf writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal that names the check, its integration point and the remaining implementation or verification work. If the rule or source needed to select a mechanism is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Delete a redundant instruction only once the structural fix enforces its rule. Preserve judgment-dependent guidance with a prominent failure example.\\n\\nPreserve explicit-invocation metadata without assuming the host enforces it. Claim enforcement, implementation or verification only for observed operations.\\n---\\nname: principle-boundary-discipline\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Boundary Discipline\\n\\nPlace validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.\\n\\n**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.\\n- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.\\n- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary's private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.\\n\\n**Applications:**\\n\\nValidation and error handling:\\n- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic\\n- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary\\n- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface\\n- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated\\n\\nCode organization:\\n- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies\\n- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state\\n- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out\\n- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results\\n\\n**The tests:**\\n- \\\"Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?\\\" If not, validation is redundant.\\n- \\\"Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?\\\" If yes, extract it.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available source access, writes and execution. Preserve user authorization and host permissions. If writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal and state which edits or checks were not performed. If required source or input contracts are missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Claim implementation and verification only from observed results.\\n\\nPreserve the explicit-invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-make-operations-idempotent\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Make Operations Idempotent\\n\\nDesign operations so they converge to the correct state regardless of how many times they run or where they start from. Every state-mutating operation should answer: \\\"What happens if this runs twice? What happens if the previous run crashed halfway?\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Commands, lifecycle operations, and processing loops run where crashes, restarts, and retries are normal. If partial state changes the next run's outcome, every restart becomes a debugging session.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- Convergent startup: scan for existing state, clean stale artifacts, adopt live sessions\\n- Content-based cleanup: compare by content equivalence, not creation order\\n- Self-healing locks: use PID-based stale lock detection\\n- Idempotent scheduling: failed work respawns cleanly, fresh input regenerated after each cycle\\n\\n**The test:**\\n1. What happens if this runs twice in a row?\\n2. What happens if the previous run crashed at every possible point?\\n3. Does re-execution converge to the same end state?\\n\\nIf any answer is \\\"it depends on what state was left behind,\\\" the operation needs a reconciliation step.\\n\\n## Capability and recovery boundaries\\n\\nUse [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to establish the tools and permissions available for inspection, execution and durable state. Apply the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) when recovery involves worker attempts or interrupted external actions.\\n\\nBefore replaying an external action, record explicit authorization, a stable action identity, its destination and the last observed outcome. Inspect the prior action and destination state after interruption. Recognize completed actions without repeating their side effects. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to that destination. An unknown outcome blocks replay. Local convergence alone does not establish external replay safety.\\n\\nIf inspection, writes, execution or persistence are unavailable, state the missing capability and provide an authorized reduced recovery design where useful. Identify checks and actions not performed; do not claim successful recovery, durable continuity or unattended execution from a design alone. Preserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-laziness-protocol\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Laziness Protocol\\n\\nAim for the most result with the least code and complexity.\\n\\n- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.\\n- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.\\n- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.\\n- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat \\\"elegant\\\" boilerplate.\\n- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.\\n- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.\\n\\n**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.\\n\\n## Capability limits\\n\\nApply this principle within the authorized task. Follow [session capability checks](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before claiming file reads, edits or verification. When writes or execution are unavailable, label the read-only proposal as reduced capability and state the missing checks. If required source is unavailable, state that the refactor cannot be assessed. Structural validation does not prove runtime behavior.\\n---\\nname: principle-minimize-reader-load\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Minimize Reader Load\\n\\nMaintainability is the work a reader must do to understand code. Track two axes:\\n1. **Layers to trace.** How many indirections sit between the question and the answer.\\n2. **State to hold.** How much hidden or mutable context the reader must keep in their head.\\n\\n**Why:** Code is read far more than it is written. LOC, cyclomatic complexity, and \\\"clean architecture\\\" are proxies. Reader load is the thing that matters. The two axes are independent. A flat file with 50 globals can be as hard to reason about as a 6-layer adapter stack. Guard both. This is the human analog of [Guard the Context Window](../principle-guard-the-context-window/SKILL.md). Working memory is finite for readers too.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- **Collapse layers** that cost more than they save: wrappers with one caller, adapters with no second implementation, speculative indirection that was never needed. Inline them.\\n- **Make adjacent layers change the abstraction.** A layer that repeats the same methods and arguments adds reader load without compression. Collapse pass-through layers.\\n- **Demand interface compression.** A broad interface that hides little complexity makes readers learn both the surface and the implementation. Prefer boundaries that hide meaningful decisions.\\n- **Shrink state scope:** prefer pure functions (returns over mutations), locals over fields, fields over module state, and module state over globals. Derive instead of sync.\\n- **Name the invariant at the boundary,** not in every consumer, so the reader learns it once.\\n- Before adding a layer or a piece of state, ask: does this reduce reader load somewhere else by at least as much?\\n\\n**The test:** Can a new reader answer \\\"where does X come from?\\\" and \\\"what can change X?\\\" in under 30 seconds? If not, cut layers or cut state.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to discover available read, write and execution tools. Inspect the concrete path, its callers and mutable state before deciding which layers to collapse. Make edits only within the authorized task and available write permissions. Run appropriate checks only through observed execution tools.\\n\\nWhen source is readable but writes or execution are denied or unavailable, give a source-grounded proposal and identify the edits or checks you could not perform. Without source or sufficient caller and state evidence, report the missing evidence and stop concrete refactoring claims. Do not claim a measured reader time without observation. Preserve invocation metadata without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-foundational-thinking\\ndescription: \\\"Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Foundational Thinking\\n\\n**Structural decisions** protect option value. **Code-level decisions** protect simplicity.\\n\\n**Data structures first.** Get the data shape right before writing logic. Define core types early, trace every access pattern, and choose structures that match the dominant paths.\\n\\nAt code level, DRY the structure, not every line. Types and data models should converge. Three similar statements still beat a premature abstraction. Prefer explicit over clever. Test behavior and edge cases, not line counts.\\n\\n**Concurrency corollary.** Before sharing state between actors, ask \\\"what happens if another actor modifies this concurrently?\\\" If not \\\"nothing\\\", isolate.\\n\\n**Scaffold first.** If something helps every later phase, do it first. Ask \\\"does every subsequent phase benefit from this existing?\\\" CI, linting, test infrastructure, and shared types are scaffold. Sequence for option value: setup before features, tests before fixes. Keep commits small and single-purpose.\\n\\nEach increment should land a coherent abstraction or deepen one that exists. Do not spread a new capability across callers as special-case coordination.\\n\\nSubtraction comes before scaffolding. Remove dead code first, then lay foundations.\\n\\n## Capability and permission boundaries\\n\\nUse the [session capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before inspecting source, editing files or running checks. Apply this principle within the authorized task. A recommendation to set up CI or make a commit grants no permission to perform it.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, give a concrete design and work sequence as reduced capability. State which edits and checks were not performed. If required source or access patterns are missing, identify them and keep any proposed shape provisional. Claim implementation or verification only after observing the authorized operation.\\n---\\nname: principle-outcome-oriented-execution\\ndescription: \\\"Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Outcome-Oriented Execution\\n\\nOptimize for the intended, verifiable end state rather than preserving smooth intermediate states.\\n\\n**Why:** Keeping every intermediate step fully stable often creates temporary compatibility code that becomes long-lived debt. Converge on the target architecture and prove correctness at explicit verification boundaries.\\n\\n**Core rule:**\\n- Prioritize end-state integrity over transitional stability\\n- Intermediate breakage is acceptable when it is planned, scoped, and reversible\\n\\n**Guardrails:**\\n- Use this for planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries\\n- Declare where temporary breakage is acceptable\\n- Keep high-signal checks for actively touched areas while migrating\\n- Require full static and runtime verification at plan completion\\n\\n## Capability and permission limits\\n\\nUse [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before inspecting source, editing files or running checks. Planned intermediate breakage stays within the authorized migration scope and host permissions. It does not authorize external actions or irreversible changes.\\n\\nIf writes or execution are unavailable, provide the target architecture, phase boundaries, acceptable reversible breakage and required verification as a reduced migration plan. Report unperformed implementation and checks explicitly. If source or the target is missing, identify the missing input before proceeding. Denied or unavailable execution leaves verification blocked; require observed full static and runtime checks before claiming plan completion.\\n\\nThe original `disable-model-invocation` metadata is retained. Its enforcement depends on the host and must not be assumed.\\n---\\nname: principle-redesign-from-first-principles\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Redesign From First Principles\\n\\nWhen integrating a change, don't bolt it onto the existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been there from the start.\\n\\n- Read all affected files and understand the current design\\n- Ask: \\\"if we were writing this from scratch with this new requirement, what would we build?\\\"\\n- Propagate the change through every reference: types, docs, examples, rationale sections\\n- Think about the whole redesign, then deliver it incrementally\\n\\nThis is the method for preserving option value when integrating changes into an existing design.\\n\\n## Capability and permission boundaries\\n\\nUse the [session capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before reading source, editing files or running checks. Apply the redesign within the authorized task. Propagating references does not grant permission to change unrelated files or perform external actions.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, provide a concrete redesign and incremental sequence as reduced capability. State which edits and checks were not performed. If affected source or design context is missing, identify the missing inputs and keep any redesign provisional. Claim implementation or verification only after observing the authorized operation.\\n---\\nname: principle-fix-root-causes\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Fix Root Causes\\n\\nWhen debugging, do not fix symptoms. Trace every problem to its root cause and fix it there.\\n\\n**Why:** Symptom fixes accumulate. Each workaround makes the system harder to reason about, and the real bug remains. Root-cause fixes are slower upfront but reduce total debugging time.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\n- Reproduce first\\n- Ask \\\"why\\\" until you hit the root cause\\n- Do not add guards (adding a nil check to silence a crash is a symptom fix)\\n- If a workaround needs a paragraph-long comment to justify it, the code is wrong (fix the code, not the comment)\\n- Check for the pattern, not just the instance (grep for the same pattern, fix all instances)\\n- When stuck, instrument. Don't guess (add logging, read the actual error)\\n\\n**Restart bugs: suspect state before code**\\n\\nWhen something \\\"fails after restart,\\\" suspect stale persistent state first: config files, caches, lock files, serialized state. If clearing a state file restores behavior, prioritize state validation as the fix.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Reproduce, instrument and fix only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. Clearing or changing persistent state also requires authorization. If reproduction, inspection or writes are unavailable or denied, state the missing capability and give the remaining investigation steps. Keep unobserved causes and fixes unverified.\\n---\\nname: principle-subtract-before-you-add\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Subtract Before You Add\\n\\nWhen evolving a system, remove complexity first, then build.\\n\\n**Why:** Adding to a complex system compounds complexity. Removing first leaves less code, reveals the essential structure, and usually makes the next design obvious. Default to subtraction.\\n\\nMake simplification a continual investment. Leave the design slightly simpler and more capable behind the same or smaller surface than you found it.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- Sequence removal before construction\\n- Cut before you polish (get to the minimum before investing in quality)\\n- Design for observed usage, not speculative edge cases\\n- No speculative validators, parsers, or guards beyond what the spec demands\\n- Simplify prompts (remove redundant instructions, excessive templates)\\n- When a reference has no novel content, delete it rather than leaving a stub\\n\\n## Session capabilities and limits\\n\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to discover available source reads, writes and execution. Remove only behavior supported as obsolete by the inspected usage and requirements, within the authorized task.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, provide an ordered removal and replacement proposal as reduced capability. State which changes and checks were not performed. If source or usage evidence is missing, identify the missing inputs before claiming removal is safe. Report only observed edits and checks.\\n\\nPreserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-prove-it-works\\ndescription: \\\"Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Prove It Works\\n\\nVerify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or \\\"it compiles.\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.\\n\\nCheck the real thing, not a proxy:\\n- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state\\n- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation\\n- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system\\n\\n## Script the check when you can\\n\\nThe strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.\\n\\nKeep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Run checks and retain artifacts only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. If direct inspection or execution is unavailable or denied, state which outputs remain unverified and withhold completion for those outputs. A proposed script is not evidence that it ran.\\n---\\nname: unslop\\ndescription: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Unslop\\n\\nEdit text to remove AI patterns.\\n\\n## Process\\n\\n1. Scan for the patterns below.\\n2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.\\n\\n## Patterns to detect and fix\\n\\nRule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.\\n\\n### Content\\n\\n3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** \\\"highlighting...\\\", \\\"ensuring...\\\", \\\"reflecting...\\\", \\\"showcasing...\\\", \\\"fostering...\\\". Delete or expand with real sources.\\n5. **Vague attributions.** \\\"Experts believe\\\", \\\"Industry reports suggest\\\", \\\"Some critics argue\\\". Name the source or delete.\\n\\n### Language\\n\\n7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.\\n8. **Fancy ways to say \\\"is\\\".** \\\"serves as\\\", \\\"stands as\\\", \\\"boasts\\\", \\\"features\\\". Just say \\\"is\\\" or \\\"has\\\".\\n9. **\\\"Not just X, but Y.\\\"** State the point directly instead.\\n10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.\\n11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.\\n12. **False ranges.** \\\"from X to Y\\\" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.\\n\\n### Style\\n\\n13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.\\n14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. \\\"If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions\\\" adds nothing with the colon. Root-cause fixes are slower upfront but reduce total debugging time.\\n\\n**Pattern:**\\n- Reproduce first\\n- Ask \\\"why\\\" until you hit the root cause\\n- Do not add guards (adding a nil check to silence a crash is a symptom fix)\\n- If a workaround needs a paragraph-long comment to justify it, the code is wrong (fix the code, not the comment)\\n- Check for the pattern, not just the instance (grep for the same pattern, fix all instances)\\n- When stuck, instrument. Don't guess (add logging, read the actual error)\\n\\n**Restart bugs: suspect state before code**\\n\\nWhen something \\\"fails after restart,\\\" suspect stale persistent state first: config files, caches, lock files, serialized state. If clearing a state file restores behavior, prioritize state validation as the fix.\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Reproduce, instrument and fix only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. Clearing or changing persistent state also requires authorization. If reproduction, inspection or writes are unavailable or denied, state the missing capability and give the remaining investigation steps. Keep unobserved causes and fixes unverified.\\n---\\nname: principle-subtract-before-you-add\\ndescription: \\\"Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Subtract Before You Add\\n\\nWhen evolving a system, remove complexity first, then build.\\n\\n**Why:** Adding to a complex system compounds complexity. Removing first leaves less code, reveals the essential structure, and usually makes the next design obvious. Default to subtraction.\\n\\nMake simplification a continual investment. Leave the design slightly simpler and more capable behind the same or smaller surface than you found it.\\n\\n**The pattern:**\\n- Sequence removal before construction\\n- Cut before you polish (get to the minimum before investing in quality)\\n- Design for observed usage, not speculative edge cases\\n- No speculative validators, parsers, or guards beyond what the spec demands\\n- Simplify prompts (remove redundant instructions, excessive templates)\\n- When a reference has no novel content, delete it rather than leaving a stub\\n\\n## Session capabilities and limits\\n\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to discover available source reads, writes and execution. Remove only behavior supported as obsolete by the inspected usage and requirements, within the authorized task.\\n\\nIf source is available but writes or execution are unavailable, provide an ordered removal and replacement proposal as reduced capability. State which changes and checks were not performed. If source or usage evidence is missing, identify the missing inputs before claiming removal is safe. Report only observed edits and checks.\\n\\nPreserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\n---\\nname: principle-prove-it-works\\ndescription: \\\"Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Prove It Works\\n\\nVerify every task output by checking the real thing directly. Do not infer from proxies, self-reports, or \\\"it compiles.\\\"\\n\\n**Why:** Unverified work has unknown correctness. Indirect verification (file mtimes, output freshness, agent self-reports, cached screenshots) feels cheaper than direct observation. Acting on a wrong inference costs far more than checking the source.\\n\\nCheck the real thing, not a proxy:\\n- Check process liveness directly, not indirectly through derived state\\n- Read the actual value, not a cached or derived representation\\n- When verification fails, suspect the observation method before suspecting the system\\n\\n## Script the check when you can\\n\\nThe strongest proof is a deterministic script that re-runs the same comparison, not a one-time eyeball. Write the script, run it, and keep its output as an artifact a reviewer can re-run instead of trusting your word.\\n\\nKeep the artifact visible for the human. Commit it only for large or complex work where the trail has to be auditable later, like a big port or migration (the **show-me-your-work** skill).\\n\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\n\\nUse the exposed tools and observed operations described in [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Run checks and retain artifacts only within the user's authorized scope and host permissions. If direct inspection or execution is unavailable or denied, state which outputs remain unverified and withhold completion for those outputs. A proposed script is not evidence that it ran.\\n\"\n    }\n  },\n  {\n    \"args\": {\n      \"cmd\": \"bun -e 'const p={\\\"doc\\\":\\\"# Filtered order CSV design\\\\n\\\\n## Problem\\\\n\\\\nCSV must represent the currently displayed rows and column order.
