Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.\\\\\\\"\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Boundary Discipline\\\\n\\\\nPlace validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.\\\\n\\\\n**Why:** Scattered validation is noisy, redundant, and gives a false sense of safety. Keep logic out of framework wiring so it can be tested without the framework.\\\\n\\\\n**The pattern:**\\\\n- **At boundaries** (CLI args, config files, external APIs, network protocols): validate, return errors, handle defensively.\\\\n- **Inside the system:** typed data, error propagation, no re-validation. Trust the types.\\\\n- **Across the boundary.** Expose domain concepts, not the boundary'\\\\''s private representation. Keep general-purpose mechanism inside and special-purpose policy at the edge.\\\\n\\\\n**Applications:**\\\\n\\\\nValidation and error handling:\\\\n- Validate config at parse time (the boundary), not inside business logic\\\\n- Parse raw data into domain types at the boundary\\\\n- Do not re-export transport, storage, framework, or wire types through the public surface\\\\n- No redundant nil checks deep in call chains if the boundary already validated\\\\n\\\\nCode organization:\\\\n- Business logic in pure functions with no framework dependencies\\\\n- Parse functions: pure transforms from raw bytes to typed state\\\\n- Prompt construction: structured state in, string out\\\\n- Scoring and assessment: pure transforms from state to results\\\\n\\\\n**The tests:**\\\\n- \\\\\\\"Is this data crossing a system boundary right now?\\\\\\\" If not, validation is redundant.\\\\n- \\\\\\\"Can this be a pure function that the shell just calls?\\\\\\\" If yes, extract it.\\\\n\\\\n## Session capabilities and permissions\\\\n\\\\nUse [the capability contract](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to check available source access, writes and execution. Preserve user authorization and host permissions. If writes or execution are unavailable, provide a reduced proposal and state which edits or checks were not performed. If required source or input contracts are missing, identify the missing inputs and keep the proposal provisional. Claim implementation and verification only from observed results.\\\\n\\\\nPreserve the explicit-invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\\\n---\\\\nname: principle-make-operations-idempotent\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\"Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.\\\\\\\"\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Make Operations Idempotent\\\\n\\\\nDesign operations so they converge to the correct state regardless of how many times they run or where they start from. Every state-mutating operation should answer: \\\\\\\"What happens if this runs twice? What happens if the previous run crashed halfway?\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n**Why:** Commands, lifecycle operations, and processing loops run where crashes, restarts, and retries are normal. If partial state changes the next run'\\\\''s outcome, every restart becomes a debugging session.\\\\n\\\\n**The pattern:**\\\\n- Convergent startup: scan for existing state, clean stale artifacts, adopt live sessions\\\\n- Content-based cleanup: compare by content equivalence, not creation order\\\\n- Self-healing locks: use PID-based stale lock detection\\\\n- Idempotent scheduling: failed work respawns cleanly, fresh input regenerated after each cycle\\\\n\\\\n**The test:**\\\\n1. What happens if this runs twice in a row?\\\\n2. What happens if the previous run crashed at every possible point?\\\\n3. Does re-execution converge to the same end state?\\\\n\\\\nIf any answer is \\\\\\\"it depends on what state was left behind,\\\\\\\" the operation needs a reconciliation step.\\\\n\\\\n## Capability and recovery boundaries\\\\n\\\\nUse [session capability discovery](../../references/host-capabilities.md) to establish the tools and permissions available for inspection, execution and durable state. Apply the [assignment and integration contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md) when recovery involves worker attempts or interrupted external actions.\\\\n\\\\nBefore replaying an external action, record explicit authorization, a stable action identity, its destination and the last observed outcome. Inspect the prior action and destination state after interruption. Recognize completed actions without repeating their side effects. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to that destination. An unknown outcome blocks replay. Local convergence alone does not establish external replay safety.\\\\n\\\\nIf inspection, writes, execution or persistence are unavailable, state the missing capability and provide an authorized reduced recovery design where useful. Identify checks and actions not performed; do not claim successful recovery, durable continuity or unattended execution from a design alone. Preserve the invocation metadata above without assuming the host enforces it.\\\\n---\\\\nname: principle-laziness-protocol\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\"Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\\\\\"\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Laziness Protocol\\\\n\\\\nAim for the most result with the least code and complexity.\\\\n\\\\n- **Prefer deletion.** When asked to refactor or improve, look for removals before additions.\\\\n- **Maintain a flat call hierarchy.** Avoid deep call chains. A rich interface that hides substantial work is not a deep call chain. If answering a question requires tracing through more than 3 files or layers, flatten it.\\\\n- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.\\\\n- **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat \\\\\\\"elegant\\\\\\\" boilerplate.\\\\n- **Question the threading.** If a task asks you to pass a new signal through types, schemas, pipelines, or similar layers, stop and look for a more direct path.\\\\n- **Sweat the small leaks.** Remove tiny pass-throughs, representation leaks, and duplicated choices before they spread. Small leaks compound into permanent coordination costs.\\\\n\\\\n**The test:** If a human developer would find the code exhausting to maintain, it is a bad solution.\\\\n\\\\n## Capability limits\\\\n\\\\nApply this principle within the authorized task. Follow [session capability checks](../../references/host-capabilities.md) before claiming file reads, edits or verification. When writes or execution are unavailable, label the read-only proposal as reduced capability and state the missing checks. If required source is unavailable, state that the refactor cannot be assessed. Structural validation does not prove runtime behavior.\\\\n\\\"}},{\\\"args\\\":{\\\"cmd\\\":\\\"cat /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/SKILL.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/runner-prompt.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/rationale-template.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/skills/architect/references/design-red-flags.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/host-capabilities.md /Users/digital-hawk/Herd/pstack-host-verification-20261016-51f209d/runtime/plugins/cache/pstack-frozen-verification/pstack-openai/0.1.3/references/model-roles.md\\\",\\\"max_output_tokens\\\":12000},\\\"result\\\":{\\\"chunk_id\\\":\\\"76bb52\\\",\\\"wall_time_seconds\\\":0.000005583,\\\"exit_code\\\":0,\\\"original_token_count\\\":6809,\\\"output\\\":\\\"---\\\\nname: architect\\\\ndescription: \\\\\\\"Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, '\\\\''architect this'\\\\'', '\\\\''design this'\\\\'', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.\\\\\\\"\\\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Architect\\\\n\\\\nDesign before implementing. Sketch types, function signatures, class shapes, and module boundaries with `not implemented` bodies and pseudocode. Synthesize across multiple model perspectives, then fill in code against the chosen sketch. If implementation proves the sketch wrong, throw it out and redesign.\\\\n\\\\n## Start\\\\n\\\\nOpen a todolist with one entry per phase before starting. If no task-list tool is exposed, keep the same phase list in the response and disclose that limit.\\\\n\\\\n1. Ground\\\\n2. Sketch\\\\n3. Agree\\\\n4. Implement\\\\n5. Scrap\\\\n\\\\n## Session capabilities and authorization\\\\n\\\\nRead [host capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use only observed exposed tools within user authorization. Read and follow each required skill in full. If direct invocation is unavailable, disclose that limit and execute its complete workflow inline as reduced capability. A missing required skill remains blocked. Record worker identities, requested and observed selections, rejections, result artifacts and limits.\\\\n\\\\nIndependent exploration requires authorized workers with observed spawn and result inspection. Without workers, disclose reduced capability and produce at least two sequential, structurally distinct alternatives using the complete arena workflow and runner discipline. Sequential alternatives are not independent model perspectives. Unverified or identical observed models do not establish model diversity. Denied source reads block grounding; denied writes leave a read-only design and an explicit implementation block.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase A: Ground the problem\\\\n\\\\nBuild a real mental model of every system the new code touches. Run the **how** skill over the relevant subsystems.\\\\n\\\\nNaming a file isn'\\\\''t grounding. Produce the traced model `how` prescribes. If the design redefines ownership or layering, also run the **why** skill on the existing shape so the rationale becomes a constraint, not a guess.\\\\n\\\\nSkip Phase A only when the work is genuinely greenfield with no surrounding system to integrate.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase B: Sketch\\\\n\\\\nRun the **arena** skill with the design-sketch task and the Phase A grounding artifacts. Pass `references/runner-prompt.md` as each runner'\\\\''s prompt. Each candidate produces a design package shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`.\\\\n\\\\nTake runner preferences from an available user-supplied `architect runners` configuration, in place of arena runner preferences. When no architect runner preferences are supplied, request inherited selection per the model-role contract. Preserve the goal of distinct model perspectives when supported and verified; inheritance does not establish diversity. Resolve aliases and rejected entries through the complete **arena** Phase A rules and current model-role contract. Select explicit models only when the exposed operation supports them; otherwise disclose inherited selection and unverified diversity. If an exact selection is required but unavailable, block that selection instead of silently replacing it.\\\\n\\\\nDesign it twice. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.\\\\n\\\\nScreen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example, and takes the shortest path that compiles. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.\\\\n\\\\nCompare viable candidates on interface depth. Prefer the design that hides more complexity behind a smaller, simpler public surface. A rich interface can keep call chains short by concentrating capability instead of scattering it across layers.\\\\n\\\\nArena returns one synthesized design package. The synthesis decision populates the rationale'\\\\''s \\\\\\\"Synthesis decision\\\\\\\" section.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase C: Agree (opt-in)\\\\n\\\\nDefault: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design when implementation is already authorized. No additional human checkpoint. Design-only scope does not authorize implementation.\\\\n\\\\nOpt in to a checkpoint when the invoker explicitly asks: \\\\\\\"/architect with checkpoint,\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\"stop and show me before implementing,\\\\\\\" or similar. Then surface the synthesized design and pause for sign-off.\\\\n\\\\nWith explicit commit authorization, the synthesis can ship as its own commit either way, as the \\\\\\\"scaffold first\\\\\\\" mode of the **foundational-thinking** principle skill. Planned and scoped breakage during fill-in is fine, per the **outcome-oriented-execution** principle skill. For adversarial pressure on the design before implementing, run the **interrogate** skill on the synthesized sketch.\\\\n\\\\nIf the human pushes back on the shape (in a checkpoint or after the fact), treat that as Phase A evidence. Re-ground and re-run Phase B before writing more code.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase D: Implement against the sketch\\\\n\\\\nReplace `not implemented` bodies with code, pseudocode with logic. The synthesized sketch is the contract.\\\\n\\\\nDeviations from the sketch are signal worth surfacing, not friction to absorb silently. If a function needs a parameter the sketch didn'\\\\''t anticipate, ask whether the sketch was wrong, the requirement was missed, or the implementation is overreaching.\\\\n\\\\n## Phase E: Scrap when the architecture is wrong\\\\n\\\\nIf implementation keeps producing friction the sketch can'\\\\''t absorb, throw the sketch out. Don'\\\\''t bolt fixes onto a wrong design, per the **redesign-from-first-principles** and **fix-root-causes** principle skills.\\\\n\\\\nThe signal is a *pattern*, not single instances. Tells:\\\\n\\\\n- The same shape of workaround appearing repeatedly across unrelated code.\\\\n- Multiple unrelated edge cases that all need special-case branches.\\\\n- Types that need escape hatches (`any`, casts, optional fields always set in practice) to compile.\\\\n- The \\\\\\\"we need a lock\\\\\\\" reflex when the sketch said the state wasn'\\\\''t shared.\\\\n- Callers having to know the abstraction'\\\\''s internal rules to use it.\\\\n- Two or more independent Phase D deviations of the same shape across the implementation.\\\\n\\\\nUse judgment. A few edge cases don'\\\\''t condemn an architecture. Some problems are legitimately complex. Complexity in the data is not complexity in the design.\\\\n\\\\nWhen you scrap:\\\\n\\\\n1. Re-run the **how** skill over what'\\\\''s been built.\\\\n2. Redesign as if the new constraints had been day-one assumptions, per redesign-from-first-principles.\\\\n3. Subtract before adding, per the **subtract-before-you-add** principle skill. The new sketch should be smaller than the old one before it grows.\\\\n4. Return to Phase B and re-run arena.\\\\n\\\\n## Outputs\\\\n\\\\nThe caller'\\\\''s usage is written first and the type sketch derived from it. One file with new types and signatures for small changes. Module map plus type definitions for larger work. The rationale ships alongside, shaped per `references/rationale-template.md`, including the usage sketch and the synthesis decision.\\\\n\\\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to generated rationale and reports without changing facts or principle meanings.\\\\n# Architect runner prompt\\\\n\\\\nThe orchestrator passes this file through to every parallel candidate runner during Phase B and fills in the variable inputs around it: the task, the Phase A grounding artifacts, the isolated working directory, and the path to write outputs. The working directory is a git worktree when available, otherwise a per-runner subdirectory under the sketch dir. What matters is independence between candidates. Create isolated directories or worktrees only with authorization and observed capabilities, following the assignment contract. Without workers, use this discipline for sequential alternatives and disclose reduced capability; do not claim independence.\\\\n\\\\nYou are producing one candidate design in architect'\\\\''s parallel exploration. Read the **architect** skill in full first. That'\\\\''s the workflow you'\\\\''re inside. Output a candidate design package: type sketch, function signatures, module map, and prose rationale shaped per [`rationale-template.md`](rationale-template.md).\\\\n\\\\nApply the following discipline. The orchestrator compares candidates on these axes to pick a base.\\\\n\\\\n- Caller'\\\\''s usage first. Write the README-style usage and two or three real call sites before the types, then derive the type sketch from them. The usage is the spec. The two must agree, so reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse.\\\\n- Data structures first. Get the core types right and the code becomes obvious. Trace each dominant access pattern through the proposed structure. If the answer is \\\\\\\"we'\\\\''ll add a map / index / cache later,\\\\\\\" the structure is wrong.\\\\n- Interface depth. Compare the capability hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface that pulls complexity into the callee, even when the implementation becomes less simple. Do not put transport or wire types on the public API. Parse into domain types behind the interface.\\\\n- Shared state: if two actors might both write, ask \\\\\\\"what happens?\\\\\\\" If the answer isn'\\\\''t \\\\\\\"nothing,\\\\\\\" default to per-actor state with a merge at the read boundary, per the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill.\\\\n- Make boundaries visible. `not implemented` errors for bodies, `// TODO` pseudocode for tricky logic, doc comments stating intent and invariants. A reader should trace data from input to output by reading types and signatures alone.\\\\n- Encode invariants in types: hard-to-misuse types > runtime checks > prose comments, per the **encode-lessons-in-structure** principle skill.\\\\n- Validate at boundaries, trust types inside, per the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. Business logic as pure functions. The shell stays thin.\\\\n- Single source of truth per invariant. Derive instead of sync.\\\\n- Idempotent state transitions where applicable, per the **make-operations-idempotent** principle skill. Ask what happens if the operation runs twice or crashes halfway.\\\\n- Short call chains. If tracing the flow needs more than three files, flatten the hierarchy, per the **laziness-protocol** and **minimize-reader-load** principle skills.\\\\n\\\\nWith observed independent workers, you are one of the parallel runners. Different models are a goal, not an assumed fact. Record requested and observed models; unknown or identical observed models do not establish diversity. In a sequential fallback, you are producing one explicitly labelled sequential alternative. Produce the best design your model can make. Don'\\\\''t hedge against the others. Differences between candidates are the signal used to pick a base and graft. Converging on a safe-looking middle defeats the exploration.\\\\n# Rationale template\\\\n\\\\nThe prose that ships alongside the type sketch. One page. Sentence-case headings, no boilerplate. Replace the italic notes with actual content.\\\\n\\\\n## Problem\\\\n\\\\n*One paragraph. What we'\\\\''re trying to do, and what about the existing system or constraints makes the shape non-obvious. If [Phase A](../SKILL.md#phase-a-ground-the-problem) surfaced constraints the design must honor (existing types to interop with, callers we can'\\\\''t break, invariants that crossed our boundary), name them here so the reader sees the same constraints you saw.*\\\\n\\\\n## Usage (caller'\\\\''s view)\\\\n\\\\n*Write this first, before the type sketch. Show the README or quickstart the consumer reads, plus two or three realistic call sites in their own code. What they import, what they call, what comes back. The type sketch in [Shape](#shape) is derived from this. The two must agree. When they diverge, reconcile the sketch to the usage, not the reverse. The caller'\\\\''s experience is the spec. The types serve it.*\\\\n\\\\n## Shape\\\\n\\\\n*The recommended architecture. Data structures first. Then how data flows through the signatures. Name the load-bearing decisions. State which invariants are encoded in types, where validation lives, and what the system deliberately does not do. Judge interface depth explicitly. State what complexity the public surface hides, what remains exposed to callers, and why the interface is no larger than needed. Cite the principle behind each decision (e.g., `per boundary-discipline`). Don'\\\\''t restate it.*\\\\n\\\\n## Synthesis decision\\\\n\\\\n*Filled in by [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Records which candidate became the base and why, what was adapted from each of the others, and what was rejected and why.*\\\\n\\\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\\\n\\\\n*One bullet per tradeoff the chosen shape makes. Form: \\\\\\\"we accept X in exchange for Y.\\\\\\\" Name anything a future reader might mistake for an oversight, including things that look like premature optimization or premature simplification.*\\\\n\\\\n## Alternatives considered\\\\n\\\\n*Required. Name at least one concrete alternative shape, with one line on why it lost. Judge each alternative on interface depth, not implementation simplicity alone. Name the complexity it exposes to callers and the complexity it hides. Two or three alternatives belong here when the design space had real contenders. One is fine when the constraints forced the answer, with the conclusion phrased as \\\\\\\"this was the only viable shape because...\\\\\\\" Avoid listing flavors of the same shape. This section covers design alternatives the chosen shape considered and rejected, not other runner candidates.*\\\\n\\\\n## Open questions and risks\\\\n\\\\n*Things you noticed during the sketch that the human needs to weigh in on, and risks worth flagging before implementation starts. Phrase as questions, not assertions, so the human'\\\\''s answer is the resolution rather than a comment.*\\\\n\\\\n## Next implementation step\\\\n\\\\n*The first thing to build against the sketch. One sentence. What you'\\\\''d start writing immediately after synthesis (or after Phase D sign-off, if a checkpoint was opted into).*\\\\n# Design red flags\\\\n\\\\nScreen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.\\\\n\\\\n## Shallow module\\\\n\\\\nA shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.\\\\n\\\\nDo not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.\\\\n\\\\nLook for these signs:\\\\n\\\\n- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.\\\\n- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.\\\\n- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.\\\\n\\\\n## Information leakage\\\\n\\\\nInformation leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.\\\\n\\\\nPublic re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.\\\\n\\\\n## Temporal decomposition\\\\n\\\\nTemporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.\\\\n\\\\nGroup code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.\\\\n\\\\n## Pass-through method\\\\n\\\\nA pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.\\\\n\\\\nRemove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.\\\\n\\\\n## Split ownership\\\\n\\\\nMore than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can'\\\\''t see the others, so their rules diverge.\\\\n\\\\nGive each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.\\\\n\\\\n## Two ways to do one task\\\\n\\\\nThe design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.\\\\n\\\\nKeep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.\\\\n\\\\n## Importable internals\\\\n\\\\nA caller can import a module'\\\\''s internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.\\\\n\\\\nMake internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.\\\\n\\\\n## Hand-synced list\\\\n\\\\nTwo or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.\\\\n\\\\nKeep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can'\\\\''t be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.\\\\n# Discover capabilities in the current session\\\\n\\\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\\\n\\\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\\\n\\\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker'\\\\''s assigned path and permissions. |\\\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker'\\\\''s terminal state after stop. |\\\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\\\n\\\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\\\n\\\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\\\n\\\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\\\n\\\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\\\n\\\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\\\n\\\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e '\\\\''const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\\\\\"python3\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"-B\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"--root\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\".\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"--commit\\\\\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\\\\\"1\\\\\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)'\\\\'' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\\\n\\\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\\\n\\\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\\\n\\\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case'\\\\''s expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\\\n\\\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\\\n\\\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\\\n\\\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. Private snapshot construction and one descriptor registry prevent importable internals and hand-synced lists. The new export contract must replace the old one in the implementation copy; exposing both would create two ways to export. B has no duplicated derived export state after revision, but still requires render coordination and adds lifecycle methods. Both keep raw JSON validation at the boundary. Neither claims an existing build mechanism for enforcing private TypeScript exports; this remains an implementation check.\\n\\n## Open questions and risks\\n\\nShould a future production integration preserve formatted display values or export underlying numeric values? The sketch uses scalar numeric values because no formatter exists in the selected source.\\n\\nWill a future UI render asynchronously? If so, can it commit the snapshot reference with the rendered table?\\n\\nIs spreadsheet-formula mitigation a product requirement? The requested CSV escaping preserves cell contents and does not silently rewrite them.\\n\\n## Next implementation step\\n\\nIn an authorized implementation copy, replace the array-only export contract with the snapshot contract and verify it through a new local fixture UI before claiming rendered behavior.\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\nDesign inspection against the selected fixture yields open rows 1 and 3 only. For displayed customer,id,total order the intended bytes are:\\n```csv\\ncustomer,id,total\\n\\\"Ada, Inc.\\\",1,12.5\\n\\\"Say \\\"\\\"Hi\\\"\\\"\\\",3,0\\n```\\nRecords use CRLF even though this Markdown display uses line breaks. An embedded customer newline remains inside a quoted cell; quotes double. A status with no matches returns the empty discriminant and no download payload. Reordered columns affect both headers and row cells. Unknown or duplicated columns fail at selection input. Two snapshot instances do not share writable state.\\n\\nThese are design-level traces, not executed feature tests. No implementation or rendered UI exists in this output. Artifact readback, digest verification and HEAD identity are the performed checks, per prove-it-works.\\n\\n# Filtered order CSV design\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nCSV must represent the currently displayed rows and column order. The supplied dashboard has two independent functions and no rendered caller. This is a design, not an existing UI or implementation.\\n\\n## Usage (caller's view)\\n\\nThese proposed call sites are written before the signatures. Shape A creates one snapshot for rendering and exporting.\\n\\n```ts\\nimport { orderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\\n// Proposed filter handler and render boundary\\nconst view = orderView(orders, 'open', ['customer', 'id', 'total']);\\nrenderTable(view.columns, view.rows);\\n// Proposed export click, capture the same snapshot used by the table\\nconst result = exportCsv(view);\\nif (result.kind === 'empty') showMessage(result.message);\\nelse download(result.csv, 'orders.csv');\\n// Proposed empty-filter handler\\nconst empty = orderView(orders, 'pending', ['id', 'customer', 'total']);\\nshowExportAvailability(empty.rows.length > 0);\\n```\\n\\nShape B has a model own the selection and export state, rather than callers retaining a view value.\\n\\n```ts\\nimport { OrdersDashboard } from './dashboard.mjs';\\nconst model = OrdersDashboard.fromOrders(orders);\\n// Proposed filter control\\nmodel.selectStatus('open');\\nmodel.displayColumns(['customer', 'id', 'total']);\\nrenderTable(model.view().columns, model.view().rows);\\n// Proposed export control\\nconst result = model.exportCsv();\\nif (result.kind === 'ready') download(result.csv, 'orders.csv');\\nelse showMessage(model.exportState().message);\\n// Proposed new filter interaction clears the previous export state\\nmodel.selectStatus('pending');\\nrenderTable(model.view().columns, model.view().rows);\\n```\\n\\n## Shape\\n\\nBoth sketches derive from the usage above. Bodies are deliberately absent. These are design notation, not source changes.\\n\\n```ts\\ntype Order = Readonly<{ id: number; status: string; customer: string; total: number }>;\\ntype ColumnKey = 'id' | 'customer' | 'total';\\ntype Columns = readonly [ColumnKey, ...ColumnKey[]];\\ntype Cell = string | number;\\ntype Column = Readonly<{ key: ColumnKey; heading: string; value: (order: Order) => Cell }>;\\ndeclare const snapshotBrand: unique symbol;\\ntype OrderViewSnapshot = Readonly<{\\n  [snapshotBrand]: true;\\n  rows: readonly Order[];\\n  columns: readonly Column[];\\n}>;\\ntype CsvResult = Readonly<{ kind: 'ready'; csv: string; rowCount: number }>\\n  | Readonly<{ kind: 'empty'; message: 'No orders match the current filter.' }>;\\n\\n/** Shape A. Exact-status filter; copied immutable rows and columns. */\\nfunction orderView(orders: readonly Order[], status: string, columns: Columns): OrderViewSnapshot {\\n  // TODO validate unique column keys at boundary; copy data; freeze snapshot.\\n  throw new Error('not implemented');\\n}\\n/** Only a factory-created view may be exported. No raw-order overload. */\\nfunction exportCsv(view: OrderViewSnapshot): CsvResult {\\n  // TODO traverse view.columns for headers and each row; escape every cell.\\n  throw new Error('not implemented');\\n}\\n\\n/** Shape B. Per-instance mutable selection; no shared global model. */\\nclass OrdersDashboard {\\n  static fromOrders(orders: readonly Order[]): OrdersDashboard { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n  selectStatus(status: string): void { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n  displayColumns(columns: Columns): void { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n  view(): OrderViewSnapshot { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n  exportCsv(): CsvResult { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n  exportState(): Readonly<{ kind: 'idle' | 'ready' | 'empty'; message: string }> { throw new Error('not implemented'); }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nA keeps the snapshot brand private. The JavaScript implementation must enforce provenance with a private WeakSet rather than relying on TypeScript alone. The factory clones row fields and column arrays so external mutation cannot change a rendered snapshot. Column descriptors come from one private registry. Their order is the supplied displayed order. The renderer consumes those same descriptors, so there is no second header list. Validate unknown JSON once at the local input boundary, and validate selectable keys on view construction. Pure filtering and serialization trust that domain data thereafter, per boundary-discipline and encode-lessons-in-structure.\\n\\nModule map for A: dashboard.mjs owns view creation, private descriptors, snapshot provenance and CSV serialization; a proposed fixture UI owns the current snapshot and download/message effects; orders.json supplies input through the UI loading boundary. A render and export trace spans only the UI and dashboard module, per laziness-protocol and minimize-reader-load. No generic CSV service or intermediate pipeline is needed. CSV is the requested final output rather than a public storage schema.\\n\\nDominant paths are linear. Filtering traverses all input orders once, rendering traverses snapshot rows and ordered columns, export traverses exactly that same snapshot. CSV wraps cells containing comma, quote, LF or CR in double quotes and doubles embedded quotes. It joins records with CRLF and preserves numeric zero. Empty rows produce the empty union case and no downloadable artifact. Repeated serialization of one snapshot returns identical bytes; repeated clicks may intentionally create repeated downloads, which belong to the shell, per make-operations-idempotent.\\n\\nB owns orders, selected status and ordered column keys in one instance. Its view and export derive from that state without separate row caches. Export state is reset on selection changes. That ownership hides synchronization, but callers must learn mutation ordering and export state lifetime. Each UI gets its own instance, per separate-before-serializing-shared-state. B needs no map or cache either.\\n\\n## Synthesis decision\\n\\nChoose A as this candidate's base. It hides filtering, descriptor selection, escaping and empty handling behind two operations while exposing only the view required by the renderer. B has deeper state ownership but six public methods and temporal rules with no supplied UI requiring them. Graft B's single ownership concern into A by requiring the UI to retain one current snapshot and export that exact value. Reject B's mutable export state because the returned union already owns the outcome. These are two sequential whole-shape sketches by one worker, not independent perspectives or a fresh judge verdict. Outer arena selection remains the coordinator's responsibility.\\n\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\n\\n- We accept copying filtered records in exchange for a stable render/export boundary.\\n- We accept passing the current snapshot from the UI in exchange for avoiding dashboard lifecycle state.\\n- We accept raw numeric totals in exchange for preserving the supplied representation; currency formatting has no supplied specification.\\n\\n## Alternatives considered\\n\\nThe OrdersDashboard model owns filter, columns and export state and hides synchronization. It loses because it exposes mutation sequencing and state lifetime that the supplied two-function module does not need. A snapshot has a smaller interface while hiding the CSV rules. Both are viable, per exhaust-the-design-space.\\n\\n## Open questions and risks\\n\\nShould a future asynchronous UI export the last committed render or the latest pending filter? This design exports the committed snapshot. Should customer fields beginning with spreadsheet formula markers be neutralized? That policy is unspecified and separate from required CSV syntax. Will future sorting or pagination define displayed rows? Such behavior must enter view construction before export; none is present in the supplied source.\\n\\n## Next implementation step\\n\\nBuild the snapshot factory and serializer against the fixture, then add a local UI that renders and exports the same snapshot.\\n\\n## Grounding and provenance\\n\\nHEAD was observed as c11649e571ac6b85d4952a532bdee95d38a38f0a. Assignment feature-arena-b, owner /root/feature_design_b, writes only outputs/arena/b. Requested model inherit-parent, actual model unknown; no native model observation or rejection exists. No nested workers are authorized. No task-list API is exposed, so this local checklist records the phases.\\n\\n- [x] Ground and frame\\n- [x] Sketch two sequential shapes\\n- [x] Compare, pick and graft within this candidate\\n- [x] Verify design artifact and assignment metadata\\n- [ ] Agree, implementation and scrap are outside design-only scope\\n\\nHow overview: committed-inputs/shared/dashboard.mjs line 1 exports visible, which filters an input array with exact status equality and returns a new array holding the original records. Line 2 exports exportCsv, which accepts any rows, writes fixed id/customer/total headers and interpolates cells without escaping. There is no call from exportCsv to visible. The entry points are exported functions; no UI trigger or rendered dashboard is supplied. orders.json contains open IDs 1 and 3, closed ID 2, a comma in Ada, Inc., an embedded quote in Say \\\"Hi\\\", and total zero. Existing functions neither own UI state nor enforce provenance. Supplied data has no newline customer, so newline handling requires a synthetic implementation test later.\\n\\nWhy coverage: source text establishes behavior, not historical intent. History beyond HEAD, PRs, tickets, documents, chat, infrastructure, exception tracking and product analytics are outside the selected-input authorization and were not searched. No motivation claim is inferred from missing evidence. Preserve exact filtering and row order; change raw export entry to snapshot export; avoid inventing an existing UI or column configuration; risk unobserved consumers when replacing the raw export signature. This is reduced source-only rationale.\\n\\n## Red-flag screen\\n\\n| Flag | A | B |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Shallow module | Two operations hide filter/column/CSV rules | Six methods hide state but expose lifecycle |\\n| Information leakage | Domain snapshot only; registry private | Domain view only; internal state private |\\n| Temporal decomposition | One immutable value | Select then render/export ordering required |\\n| Pass-through method | Neither operation forwards unchanged arguments | view derives state; no separate forwarding layer |\\n| Split ownership | UI owns one snapshot; exporter pure | One instance owns state; no UI copies allowed |\\n| Two ways to export | Replace raw-row export, no overload | One export method, remove old path |\\n| Importable internals | Helpers non-exported; brand/provenance private | Instance internals private |\\n| Hand-synced list | One descriptor registry | Same registry used by model and export |\\n\\nImplementation integration must remove the old raw export path and migrate any newly discovered callers together, rather than retaining two methods. No caller removal is claimed here. Repeated design deviations would trigger re-grounding and redesign, per redesign-from-first-principles and fix-root-causes; subtraction precedes adding a controller, per subtract-before-you-add.\\n\\n## Verification boundary\\n\\nDesign review traces open rows 1 and 3 through each shape and excludes closed row 2. With customer/id/total displayed order, expected records are customer,id,total; then \\\"Ada, Inc.\\\",1,12.5; then \\\"Say \\\"\\\"Hi\\\"\\\"\\\",3,0. A pending status yields empty feedback. Proposed implementation checks must include CR and LF quoting, column reorder and subset, external mutation after snapshot, and filter change between renders. No feature execution, UI screenshot or automated behavior pass is claimed. Artifact readback and SHA256 verify delivery only, per prove-it-works.\\n\\n## Read principle leaves\\n\\nAll paths below are relative to the authorized frozen package skills directory, read in full. foundational-thinking guided data-first sketches; outcome-oriented-execution applies only to later implementation boundaries. Remaining decisions cite their relevant leaves above.\\n\\n- principle-exhaust-the-design-space/SKILL.md\\n- principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md\\n- principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md\\n- principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md\\n- principle-make-operations-idempotent/SKILL.md\\n- principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md\\n- principle-minimize-reader-load/SKILL.md\\n- principle-foundational-thinking/SKILL.md\\n- principle-outcome-oriented-execution/SKILL.md\\n- principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md\\n- principle-fix-root-causes/SKILL.md\\n- principle-subtract-before-you-add/SKILL.md\\n- principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md\\n\\nFrozen architect, runner prompt, rationale template, red flags, how, why, arena, capability/model/ownership/assignment contracts and unslop were read. Unslop was applied without altering facts. No rubric or sibling candidate was read.\\n---\\nname: arena\\ndescription: \\\"Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.\\\"\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\n---\\n\\n# Arena\\n\\nRead [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md), [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), and [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Use only exposed, authorized operations. Read each applied principle leaf in full before dependent work. Missing required reads block that work. Invocation aliases are guidance, not proof of registered host commands.\\n\\nIndependent candidates and a fresh independent judge require observed worker operations and inspected artifacts. If unavailable, produce authorized sequential alternatives and parent comparison only as reduced capability. Do not claim independence, background execution, model diversity or a full arena pass. If independence is required, leave that gate blocked.\\n\\nFan out N parallel attempts at the same task. Read every candidate end to end. Pick the strongest as the base. Graft the best ideas from the others into it. Verify the synthesized result.\\n\\n## Start\\n\\nOpen an exposed todo list with one entry per phase before launching anything. Without one, use an authorized local Markdown checklist and disclose the reduced binding.\\n\\n1. Frame\\n2. Fan out\\n3. Cross-judge\\n4. Pick\\n5. Graft\\n6. Verify\\n\\n## Phase A: Frame\\n\\nThe N candidates will receive the same prompt, so the prompt is the contract.\\n\\n1. State the artifact each candidate is producing.\\n2. Derive the rubric. State what success looks like for *this* task, then turn it into 3-6 concrete gradeable criteria. The rubric is the picker's tool in Phase D. Candidates only see the task.\\n3. Pick the runners. Use an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena runners` preference if available. Otherwise request two inherited workers, one per seat. The source defaults used two specific model families. Their source-host slugs are not portable availability evidence. Select an explicit model or effort only from current exposed documentation or observed enumeration under the model-role contract. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry means omit explicit model selection. On rejection, record it and disclose a supported same-family alternative when available, otherwise an authorized inherited alternative. If the exact model is required, block instead. Record requested and observed model and effort separately, using unknown when unobserved. More seats can cover multiple design directions. Same model N times is appropriate when work is generation-bound rather than judgment-sensitive. Unknown models leave diversity unverified.\\n4. Assign output paths. Each candidate writes to its own authorized location, a git worktree where supported, otherwise a distinct local candidate directory. Follow [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Confirm isolation and write permissions before dispatch. Record immutable assignment identity, input SHA, owner, role and evidence links under the assignment contract. Workers never integrate shared files. Worktree creation and persistence require observed authorized capabilities.\\n\\n## Phase B: Fan out\\n\\nDispatch all N independent candidates together through the exposed worker operation, using observed background execution when available. Give each the same task, shared grounding path, its isolated output path, and instructions to produce both the artifact and a short rationale. Withhold the rubric from candidates. Inspect terminal results and artifact paths before accepting completion; a wait notification alone is insufficient.\\n\\nEach rationale names the alternatives the candidate considered and what it rejected.\\n\\nIf a candidate fails to produce output, proceed with N-1 and note the dropout in the synthesis record. One survivor means incomplete competition, even if its artifact is useful. Zero survivors blocks synthesis. Never integrate partial or cancelled artifacts as completed candidates.\\n\\n## Phase C: Cross-judge\\n\\nAfter all Phase B candidates reach terminal state and their accepted artifacts are inspected, choose one model from an explicitly supplied, authorized `arena cross-judge pool` preference. Without that preference, use an inherited worker or a supported explicit selection under the model-role contract. The source pool named the same two families as the runners; it does not establish portable model availability. Prefer a different observed model family from the parent's when available. Disclose rejected choices and supported fallbacks, or block if the exact choice is required.\\n\\nSpawn one fresh readonly judge worker. It sees the rubric and completed candidates by path label, scores each criterion, and recommends a base with rationale. It runs in parallel with the parent's reading in Phase D when observed background execution permits it, never with candidates still writing. The judge has no candidate write ownership. Unknown actual models leave diversity unverified. Unavailable fresh judging remains a reduced or blocked gate, never an invented independent verdict.\\n\\n## Phase D: Pick a base\\n\\nRead every candidate end to end before picking.\\n\\nScore each candidate against the rubric criterion by criterion, not on holistic feel. Compare against the cross-judge. Agreement on the base confirms the pick. Disagreement means one of you is biased or the rubric was ambiguous. Read both rationales before deciding.\\n\\nPick the base on which candidate a future maintainer can extend most easily without breaking invariants. Prefer the cleaner boundary or smaller API when two feel tied, per the [Laziness Protocol](../principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md).\\n\\nRecord the pick and the reason in a short synthesis note alongside the base artifact, including the cross-judge's verdict.\\n\\n## Phase E: Graft\\n\\nWalk each losing candidate once more and identify what is worth porting into the base. The signal is usually one or two things per candidate, not most of it.\\n\\nFold each graft in by hand, per [redesign-from-first-principles](../principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md). Don't paste mechanically. The result has to remain coherent under one mental model.\\n\\nRecord what was grafted, from which candidate, and what was rejected and why.\\n\\nWhen N candidates converge on the same shape, that is a strong agreement signal. Note the convergence in the record and deliver the consensus shape within authorized scope. No graft is needed. When N candidates wildly diverge, Phase A was under-specified. Reframe and re-run rather than averaging the divergence.\\n\\n## Phase F: Verify\\n\\nThe synthesized artifact has to hold up under the same scrutiny as any other output, per [prove-it-works](../principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md).\\n\\nIf verification surfaces a problem the arena did not catch, either Phase A was wrong (re-frame and re-run) or one candidate caught it and you missed the graft (go back to Phase E). Don't paper over.\\n\\nApply [unslop](../unslop/SKILL.md) to the synthesis prose. External publication, commits, messages and setup require their own authorization.\\n\\n## Outputs\\n\\nOne synthesized artifact. One short synthesis note alongside, naming the base, the grafts and their source candidates, the rejections, the dropouts if any, and the verification result.\\n# Discover capabilities in the current session\\n\\nRead the tools exposed to this session before assigning work. Cached official-subagents.txt is documentation context; it proves no operation succeeded. Local agent configuration is not portable plugin configuration.\\n\\nRecord each binding as `{operation, tool, exposed, succeeded, evidence, limits}`. `tool` is the exact exposed identifier or null when absent. `succeeded` is true only after observing a result. Keep failed and unavailable bindings. Successful bindings become `successfulOperations` in host evidence, with a root-relative evidence file. The operation labels below describe purposes, never callable APIs.\\n\\n| Operation | Discovery and observation required |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| spawn | Find an exposed independent-worker operation; retain returned worker identity and exact assigned revision. |\\n| follow-up | Find the operation that sends input to that worker; observe acceptance by the same identity. |\\n| wait | Find the operation that waits for worker state; retain terminal or interrupted state. |\\n| inspect-result | Read the worker result and its referenced artifacts; a wait notification alone is insufficient. |\\n| stop | Observe cancellation or termination through the exposed operation. |\\n| read | Observe the requested file content through the available file tool. |\\n| isolated-write | Observe a write within the worker's assigned path and permissions. |\\n| history | Observe available prior turns or records; declare gaps explicitly. |\\n| execution | Observe command execution with exit status and output. |\\n| persistence | Write and read an authorized durable record; a claimed save is insufficient. |\\n| external-write | Record explicit authorization and action identity; inspect the result before replay. |\\n| resolve-ownership | Observe distinct owned paths before contested writes. |\\n| inspect-terminal | Observe the worker's terminal state after stop. |\\n| quarantine-artifacts | Observe partial artifacts withheld from integration. |\\n| inspect-prior-action | Read the interrupted action identity and prior outcome. |\\n| inspect-destination | Observe the destination state for that action identity. |\\n| safe-recovery | Observe explicitly authorized idempotent recovery after identity and destination inspection. |\\n\\nNo default API names are assigned here. Tool names differ by host and session. An exposed tool may still be denied or fail. Record requested and actual models only when observed; otherwise use `unknown`. A requested model never proves the actual model.\\n\\nA denied or unavailable operation blocks the branch that requires it. Sequential substitution for required independent work is reduced capability and uses `reduced-pass`; ordinary direct completion can fully pass. Missing persistence limits session pickup even when current work succeeds. Preserve user authorization and host permission boundaries through every fallback.\\n\\nWorker passes require observed spawn and result inspection. Each registry entry declares `requiredObservations` for `pass` and `reduced-pass`; tool observations need exposed bindings and existing evidence artifacts; native text observations use the separate reviewed native record below. Full cancellation requires stop, terminal inspection and artifact quarantine. Full persistence requires durable write and readback. Full interrupted-action recovery requires prior identity inspection, destination inspection, safe recovery, explicit external permission and a recorded prior action identity even when no external-write observation is listed.\\n\\nPermission checks follow performed operations. Isolated writes and persistence require granted writes. External writes and safe recovery require granted external permission and prior identity. Authorized read-only reductions may retain denied writes; their limits must preserve denied or unavailable permissions. Required observations remain applicable to those reductions.\\n\\nHost evidence is stored as object or array JSON files under `docs/parity/evidence/`. Required fields are defined by `docs/parity/evidence.schema.json`. Artifacts and operation evidence must be existing files inside the tested root. Test fixtures belong in `tests/` and prove validator behavior only.\\n\\nRun `python3 tools/validate_evidence.py --root . --commit <tested-package-commit>` through Bun, for example `bun -e 'const p=Bun.spawnSync([\\\"python3\\\",\\\"-B\\\",\\\"tools/validate_evidence.py\\\",\\\"--root\\\",\\\".\\\",\\\"--commit\\\",process.argv[1]],{env:{...process.env,PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE:\\\"1\\\"}});process.stdout.write(p.stdout);process.stderr.write(p.stderr);process.exit(p.exitCode)' <tested-package-commit>`. It reads every JSON record below the evidence directory, prints each error, and exits 1 for invalid records or 0 for valid records. An empty directory has no invalid records and supplies no behavioral evidence.\\n\\nThe required registry file in `docs/parity/case-registry.json` declares applicability. Missing or non-file registry, unknown case, structural-only entry or unlisted host rejects behavioral validation. Maintenance fixtures use a temporary copy of this registry; they cannot bypass applicability. Required hosts must receive observed evidence or explicit blocked records before release claims. Structural checks have no required host and cannot populate host status. Later producers propose task-owned entries; only the coordinator integrates them. Source paths select callers through the task 3 case contract. Case definitions alone leave host statuses `not-run`.\\n\\n## Direct completion and recorded observations\\n\\n`direct` means the task is completed in the current context. Restatement, supplied-text writing and complete installed discovery can pass directly. `sequential` is reserved for replacing a required independent method with sequential work and remains reduced. A text response has no invented callable tool. Record supplied input, the actual response and qualitative outcome review as `nativeObservations`, each with its existing listed evidence artifact and named reviewer. Their labels are `supplied-input`, `response` and `review-outcome`. The reviewer assesses the case's expected outcome; validation checks evidence relationships and does not decide prose quality.\\n\\nEach registry entry declares allowed execution modes and required permissions for each status. A grant is required for the performed action: worker spawn, command execution and stop need execution; isolated output or persistence needs writes; external actions need their separate permission and prior identity. Read-only discovery does not inherit an execution grant requirement. Tool observations still name an actually exposed tool and existing evidence. Native observations cannot claim tool discovery, worker identity or saved writes.\\n\\nFull Arena and Swarm results additionally provide `inputRevision` and a listed `methodReceipt` artifact. An exposed `inspect-method` operation must reference that receipt. Assignment operations name `assignmentId` and the corresponding inspected output. See the [structured method contract](orchestration-contract.md). All positive maintenance fixtures are synthetic; none is an observed host result.\\n# Model selection for portable roles\\n\\nUse [session capabilities](host-capabilities.md) before assigning a role. These [poteto](agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and [comment reviewer](agent-prompts/comment-sicko.md) prompts are instructions supplied to an exposed worker operation. Reading them does not register a custom agent or authorize delegation.\\n\\n| Role | Default requested model | Observed model | Supported effort | Fallback disclosure |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| poteto-agent | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n| comment-sicko | inherit-parent | unknown until observed | inherit-parent unless a supported explicit effort is verified | Record rejected selection, replacement request, observed result and limits. |\\n\\nFor each assignment, record requested model and effort, observed model and effort, supported effort values and their source, worker identity, and fallback disclosure. Use `unknown` for information the operation does not expose. `inherit-parent` records a selection policy, not an observed model name. Do not silently convert a requested model into an actual model.\\n\\nSelect an explicit model only from current exposed tool documentation or observed enumeration results. If enumeration is missing, disclose that limit and retain `inherit-parent`. Documentation examples are not a list of available models. Use only an effort supported for the selected model by the current operation; do not carry an incompatible inherited effort into an explicit selection.\\n\\nIf a selected model or effort is rejected, retain the rejection. Use an authorized inherited or supported alternative only after disclosing the changed selection. If the task requires that exact selection, stop and record blocked. A fallback never proves the original selection succeeded.\\n\\nIdentical observed models mean no model diversity. Different roles can supply distinct instructions on the same model. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified, even when requested model names differ. Different observed models support a model-diversity statement only for those observed assignments. Worker independence still requires successful spawn and result inspection.\\n\\nWhen workers are unavailable, apply an authorized role sequentially and label reduced capability. Preserve scope and permission boundaries. Do not claim independent review, background execution, or full worker support from sequential role switching.\\n\\nThe cached documentation from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents describes inheritance and optional local agent configuration. It is context only. This package writes no local custom-agent configuration and claims no current host model or worker support from that documentation.\\n# Assignment and integration contract\\n\\nBefore dispatch, the coordinator creates an immutable assignment with `id`, `scope`, `inputRevision`, `outputOwner`, `isolatedOutputPath`, `role`, `retryCount`, `terminalStatus`, and `evidenceLinks`. Use the full Git SHA for inputRevision, an exact owned path, and an explicit role. Start retryCount at 0 and terminalStatus at `pending`. Preserve every attempt as an append-only event under the same assignment ID; update status through events, never rewrite the original scope, revision, owner or path. A changed scope or revision requires a new assignment ID that links its predecessor.\\n\\nThe coordinator checks authorization and observed host bindings before dispatch. One path has one writer. Reject overlapping paths before work starts; assign distinct paths instead. Workers write only their isolated output and report results. Only the coordinator integrates shared files, inventory, registry, or other workers' output.\\n\\nAccept a result only when its assignment identity and input SHA match, its artifacts exist, and required method evidence was observed. Reject stale revisions. Permit at most one retry for missing required SHA or method evidence, after inspecting the prior attempt and confirming the same permissions still apply. A retry count of 1 exhausts this allowance. Denied permissions, unknown action outcomes, and missing artifacts never become success by retry policy.\\n\\nTerminal states are `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. A completion event links the exact result and evidence. Stop a cancelled worker through the exposed stop binding when available, then inspect its terminal state. Quarantine any partial artifacts; cancellation does not authorize their integration. If stop cannot be observed, record that limit and do not claim termination. Report interrupted execution explicitly.\\n\\nBefore an external action, record explicit permission, a stable action identity, the intended destination and the last observed outcome. After interruption, inspect whether that identity already completed. Retry only with authorization, an observed safe replay decision and an idempotency mechanism appropriate to the destination. If the outcome is unknown, block replay. Do not infer permission from upstream autonomy instructions.\\n\\nHistory and persistence have separate bindings. Keep assignment events and result links in an authorized durable location and verify readback. If unavailable, declare the gap and offer an authorized local handoff as reduced capability; never claim unattended recovery or cross-session continuity.       "text": "# CSV export design\n\n## Usage (caller's view)\n\nShape A shares one immutable OrderViewSnapshot between rendering and export. Rendering and export use this same value.\nview = createOrderView(orders, { status: \"closed\", columns: view.columns.map(c => c.key) });\nrenderTable(view.columns, view.rows);\n\n// Export click captures the displayed view synchronously.\nconst result = exportCsv(view);\nif (result.kind === \"empty\") showNotice(result.message);\nelse downloadCsv(result.csv, \"orders.csv\");\n```\n\nShape B instead makes an OrdersDashboard instance the state owner.\n\n```ts\nconst dashboard = new OrdersDashboard(orders, { status: \"open\", columns: [\"customer\", \"id\", \"total\"] });\nrenderTable(dashboard.view().columns, dashboard.view().rows);\ndashboard.setStatus(\"closed\"); renderTable(dashboard.view().columns, dashboard.view().rows);\nconst exportState = dashboard.exportCurrent();\nif (exportState.kind === \"ready\") downloadCsv(exportState.csv, \"orders.csv\");\nelse showNotice(exportState.message);\n```\n\n## Problem\n\nThe supplied dashboard.mjs has two independent functions. visible filters by exact status equality. exportCsv serializes every row it receives using fixed id,customer,total order and interpolates cell values without quoting. Rows contain copied scalar values so later mutation of the original JSON objects cannot alter the displayed export.\n\n```ts\ntype Order = Readonly<{ id: number; status: string; customer: string; total: number }>;\ntype ColumnKey = \"id\" | \"customer\" | \"total\";\ntype OrderColumn = Readonly<{ key: ColumnKey; label: string }>;\ntype ExportResult =\n  | Readonly<{ kind: \"empty\"; message: \"No orders match the current filter.\" }>\n  | Readonly<{ kind: \"ready\"; csv: string; rowCount: number }>;\ndeclare const snapshotBrand: unique symbol;\ntype OrderViewSnapshot = Readonly<{\n  [snapshotBrand]: true;\n  rows: readonly Order[];\n  columns: readonly OrderColumn[];\n}>;\ntype ViewSelection = Readonly<{ status: string; columns: readonly ColumnKey[] }>;\n\nfunction createOrderView(orders: readonly Order[], selection: ViewSelection): OrderViewSnapshot {\n  // TODO Validate selection at public boundary; reject empty or duplicate columns.\n  // TODO Use exact status equality; copy and freeze selected scalar rows.\n  // TODO Resolve descriptors from one private registry, in selection order.\n  throw new Error(\"not implemented\");\n}\nfunction exportCsv(view: OrderViewSnapshot): ExportResult {\n  // TODO Return empty before creating a file when rows.length is zero.\n  // TODO Use view.columns for both headers and every row, preserving order.\n  // TODO Quote fields containing comma, quote, CR or LF; double embedded quotes.\n  // TODO Join records with CRLF; preserve newlines inside quoted values.\n  throw new Error(\"not implemented\");\n}\n```\n\nThe JSON-loading boundary must validate unknown records into Order values once, including finite numeric totals and string customers.
