      "text": "# Code owner checkpoint\n\nAssignment feature-code-0. Owner /root/feature_code. Input c11649e571ac6b85d4952a532bdee95d38a38f0a. Requested model and effort inherit-parent. Observed model and effort unknown. Writes restricted to outputs/working. No nested workers or Git mutations. Local checklist is the reduced todo binding. Lead owns steps 1, 2, 4 review and integration.\n\n1. Run [how](../../how/SKILL.md) over the affected subsystem. Ground the intended user outcome in traced source and caller behavior.\n2. Run [architect](../../architect/SKILL.md) for parallel design exploration. Follow its complete design and arena contracts. Preserve sequential alternatives only as reduced capability when independent workers are unavailable. Required independence remains blocked.\n3. Write the throughput checkpoint as four todo items. Keep any dimension that does not apply, such as a single file or no fan-out, with `n/a: <reason>` rather than dropping it.\n   - Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\n   - Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services, or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\n   - Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using [separate-before-serializing-shared-state](../../principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md). Serialize only for real invariants.\n   - Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\n4. Delegate code-writing to a fresh independent worker with the entire [poteto role prompt](../../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) and exact file pointers. Use the configured feature role when supported and observed. Otherwise request inherited model and effort. Record requested and observed selections separately, with unknown for unobserved values. Assign exact file paths, a named data shape and its organizing structure, and success criteria tied to the user outcome. Choose the structure before the delegate writes logic under [model-the-domain](../../principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md). Prefer a state machine over scattered booleans, a table or registry over branching, or a typed model over repeated shape assumptions. When implementation admits multiple valid shapes, such as error handling, abstraction layer or test structure, delegate through [arena](../../arena/SKILL.md). Its runners surface alternatives and its fresh cross-judge guards the pick. This gate is mandatory. There is no skip-with-reason escape, and Laziness Protocol does not override it. The gain is review separation, not lines saved. A worker forbidden to spawn owns the diff directly and returns it to the lead for the same review separation. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \"standing by\". Without authorized independent workers, direct implementation can be an explicit reduced result, but it does not satisfy independent review separation. The lead reviews the actual diff and owns the summary. Apply the mode's Comments rules. Make surgical edits and re-ground upstream-derived files against their source. Port shared-primitive improvements to all consumers and verify each. Commit each verified unit when authorized and after the mode's commit gates.\n5. Verify on the matching surface using available authorized control tools and the mode's matching companion requirements. Tie observed evidence to the intended user outcome. \"Inconclusive\" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it and retain the unverified gate. Compilation or structural checks do not prove the feature works.\n6. Rebase into small, ordered commits and stack follow-ups when authorized and safe for concurrent work. Use [sequence-verifiable-units](../../principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md). Build, verify and commit each small unit before the next. An unrun required check blocks advancement. If commit or rebase is unavailable or unauthorized, return the checked diff and ordered delivery plan with those operations unperformed.\n7. If the design is contested, run [interrogate](../../interrogate/SKILL.md) before shipping. Preserve its review rubric, independence and observed model-diversity limits. Sequential review does not become independent or multi-model review.\n8. Run the Opening a PR playbook at `opening-a-pr.md` in this directory. This caller requires that complete playbook, its review gates and actual PR result inspection. If the file is absent, report the exact deferred dependency and stop PR-dependent work. Do not reconstruct it from this paragraph. External PR creation and push require actual authorization. Return a local reviewable result when those actions are unavailable or unauthorized. Never claim a local draft is a created PR. Opening a PR does not start Babysit.\n\n\n## Before unit1\n- Blocking first steps. Required mode, role, Feature, principles and synthesis read. Exact HEAD checked.\n- Independent workstreams. n/a, this owner implements the coupled module and UI.\n- Shared mutable state. Sole writer in outputs/working. Originals stay untouched.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. Unit1 snapshot and CSV, execute checks, then unit2 UI.\n\n## After unit1, before unit2\n- Blocking first steps. Bun unit1 passed with literal expected records and CSV bytes.\n- Independent workstreams. n/a, UI depends on the now-checked module.\n- Shared mutable state. UI owns one current snapshot. Root reviews after this owner returns.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. Add the local UI, then rerun unit1 and UI contract checks. Browser checks remain open.\n\n## After unit2\n- Blocking first steps. Unit1 passed before UI writes. Unit1 and static UI contract checks passed after unit2.\n- Independent workstreams. n/a, implementation is ready for the lead's separate review.\n- Shared mutable state. No original inputs changed. Only this owner's working directory changed.\n- Smallest safe decomposition. Ordered checked diff is complete. Browser controls and companion gates remain open.\n\n## Result\nThe local Orders page now filters by exact status and exports its current immutable snapshot. The CSV uses displayed customer, id and total order. Empty selection shows a useful message and does not prepare a file. Record delimiters are CRLF. Values containing commas, quotes, CR or LF use CSV quoting. Embedded quotes double.\n\nThe next maintainer inherits one domain module with createOrderView and exportCsv. The raw-array export path is replaced in the working copy. Model the Domain shaped the snapshot and private column registry. Separate Before Serializing Shared State kept this output under one writer. Sequence Work into Verifiable Units required unit1 to pass before UI changes. Prove It Works produced repeatable literal checks.\n\nRun `bun --no-install outputs/working/check.mjs --ui` from the case root. The first output line proves pure domain behavior against literal expected values. The second line covers a static HTML contract. It does not prove browser rendering, filter events, real download bytes or browser console behavior. Serve outputs/working using an authorized local static server for browser review. Direct file URLs may block fetch.\n\nNo comments were added. Required deslop, no-comments companion and matching control companions remain unmet. Root owns independent review and any browser checks. No install, external service, commit, rebase, push, PR or production verification occurred. Observed model and effort remain unknown. Formula neutralization and formatted display values remain future product policies. The fixture preserves literal values.\n"

      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/working/orders.json",

      "sha256": "561bca1cb0c759f9785ae826d8285fab84f0d419760917709a7f44968d10ee93",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "[\n  {\n    \"id\": 1,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Ada, Inc.\",\n    \"total\": 12.5\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 2,\n    \"status\": \"closed\",\n    \"customer\": \"Hidden\",\n    \"total\": 4\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 3,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Say \\\"Hi\\\"\",\n    \"total\": 0\n  }\n]"
    },
    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/working/dashboard.mjs",
      "bytes": 1843,
      "sha256": "eb977927ba8643c9dc07704daedc01a2482a2eacd8762b24773bc110d0398de9",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "const registry = Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(['id', 'customer', 'total'].map(key => [key, Object.freeze({ key, label: key })])));\nconst snapshots = new WeakSet();\n\nexport function createOrderView(orders, { status, columns }) {\n  if (!Array.isArray(orders) || typeof status !== 'string' || !Array.isArray(columns) || !columns.length || new Set(columns).size !== columns.length || columns.some(key => !Object.hasOwn(registry, key))) {\n    throw new TypeError('Expected orders, a status and unique supported columns.');\n  }\n  const copied = orders.map(order => {\n    if (!order || typeof order.id !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.id) || typeof order.customer !== 'string' || typeof order.status !== 'string' || typeof order.total !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.total)) {\n      throw new TypeError('Invalid order record.');\n    }\n    return Object.freeze({ id: order.id, customer: order.customer, total: order.total, status: order.status });\n  });\n  const snapshot = Object.freeze({\n    rows: Object.freeze(copied.filter(order => order.status === status)),\n    columns: Object.freeze(columns.map(key => registry[key]))\n  });\n  snapshots.add(snapshot);\n  return snapshot;\n}\n\nexport function exportCsv(snapshot) {\n  if (!snapshots.has(snapshot)) throw new TypeError('Expected an OrderViewSnapshot.');\n  if (!snapshot.rows.length) return Object.freeze({ kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\n  const cell = value => /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(String(value)) ? `\"${String(value).replaceAll('\"', '\"\"')}\"` : String(value);\n  const lines = [snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(column.label)).join(',')];\n  for (const row of snapshot.rows) lines.push(snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(row[column.key])).join(','));\n  return Object.freeze({ kind: 'ready', csv: lines.join('\\r\\n'), rowCount: snapshot.rows.length });\n}\n"
    },

    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/working/check.mjs",
      "bytes": 2535,
      "sha256": "9da8ef5006034013a392eb696b5de7f404aeb8b75b617a644cf861402b95d57c",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst orders = await Bun.file(new URL('./orders.json', import.meta.url)).json();\nconst view = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\nassert.deepEqual(view.rows.map(row => row.id), [1, 3]);\nassert.deepEqual(view.columns.map(column => column.key), ['customer', 'id', 'total']);\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(view), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'customer,id,total\\r\\n\"Ada, Inc.\",1,12.5\\r\\n\"Say \"\"Hi\"\"\",3,0', rowCount: 2 });\nconst subset = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'closed', columns: ['total', 'customer'] });\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(subset), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'total,customer\\r\\n4,Hidden', rowCount: 1 });\nconst special = createOrderView([{ id: 9, customer: 'A\\rB\\n\"C\",D', total: 0, status: 'open' }], { status: 'open', columns: ['customer'] });\nassert.equal(exportCsv(special).csv, 'customer\\r\\n\"A\\rB\\n\"\"C\"\",D\"');\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(createOrderView(orders, { status: 'missing', columns: ['id'] })), { kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\norders[0].customer = 'changed';\nassert.equal(view.rows[0].customer, 'Ada, Inc.');\nassert.throws(() => { view.rows[0].customer = 'changed'; }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => { view.columns.reverse(); }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => exportCsv({ ...view }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['id', 'id'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['status'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView([{ id: 1, status: 'open', customer: 'x', total: NaN }], { status: 'open', columns: ['id'] }), TypeError);\nconsole.log('unit1 pass: exact rows, order, CSV bytes, escaping, subset, empty, mutation and boundary rejection');\nif (process.argv.includes('--ui')) {\n  const html = await Bun.file(new URL('./index.html', import.meta.url)).text();\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"exportCsv(currentView)\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"currentView = nextView\"));\n  assert.ok(html.indexOf('rows.replaceChildren(body)') < html.indexOf('currentView = nextView'));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total']\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"notice.textContent = result.message\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"link.download = 'orders.csv'\"));\n  assert.equal(html.includes('innerHTML'), false);\n  console.log('unit2 pass: static local UI contract only; browser interaction and actual download unverified');\n}\n"

      "text": "<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n<title>Orders CSV 0}button{background:#174c60;color:white;border:0;border-radius:4px}table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;background:white}th,td{text-align:left;padding:14px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dfe4}#notice{min-height:24px}\n</style>\n<h1>Orders</h1>\n<label for=\"status\">Status</label>\n<select id=\"status\"><option value=\"open\">Open</option><option value=\"closed\">Closed</option><option value=\"missing\">No matching orders</option></select>\n<button id=\"export\" type=\"button\" disabled>Export CSV</button>\n<p id=\"notice\" role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\">Loading orders...</p>\n<table aria-label=\"Current orders\"><thead id=\"head\"></thead><tbody id=\"rows\"></tbody></table>\n<script type=\"module\">\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst status = document.querySelector('#status');\nconst exportButton = document.querySelector('#export');\nconst notice = document.querySelector('#notice');\nconst head = document.querySelector('#head');\nconst rows = document.querySelector('#rows');\nlet currentView;\nlet orders;\nfunction render() {\n  const nextView = createOrderView(orders, { status: status.value, columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\n  const header = document.createElement('tr');\n  for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n    const cell = document.createElement('th');\n    cell.scope = 'col';\n    cell.textContent = column.label;\n    header.append(cell);\n  }\n  const body = document.createDocumentFragment();\n  for (const order of nextView.rows) {\n    const row = document.createElement('tr');\n    for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n      const cell = document.createElement('td');\n      cell.textContent = String(order[column.key]);\n      row.append(cell);\n    }\n    body.append(row);\n  }\n  head.replaceChildren(header);\n  rows.replaceChildren(body);\n  currentView = nextView;\n  notice.textContent = currentView.rows.length ? `${currentView.rows.length} orders shown.` : 'No orders match the current filter.';\n}\nstatus.addEventListener('change', render);\nexportButton.addEventListener('click', () => {\n  const result = exportCsv(currentView);\n  if (result.kind === 'empty') {\n    notice.textContent = result.message;\n    return;\n  }\n  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([result.csv], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' }));\n  const link = document.createElement('a');\n  link.href = url;\n  link.download = 'orders.csv';\n  document.body.append(link);\n  link.click();\n  link.remove();\n  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);\n  notice.textContent = `CSV prepared for ${result.rowCount} orders.`;\n});\ntry {\n  const response = await fetch('./orders.json');\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load orders.');\n  orders = await response.json();\n  render();\n  exportButton.disabled = false;\n} catch (error) {\n  notice.textContent = `Orders unavailable. ${error.message}`;\n  status.disabled = true;\n}\n</script>\n</html>\n"

    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/variants/browser-verification-denied/working/orders.json",
      "bytes": 269,
      "sha256": "561bca1cb0c759f9785ae826d8285fab84f0d419760917709a7f44968d10ee93",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "[\n  {\n    \"id\": 1,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Ada, Inc.\",\n    \"total\": 12.5\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 2,\n    \"status\": \"closed\",\n    \"customer\": \"Hidden\",\n    \"total\": 4\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 3,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Say \\\"Hi\\\"\",\n    \"total\": 0\n  }\n]"
    },
    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/variants/browser-verification-denied/working/dashboard.mjs",
      "bytes": 1843,
      "sha256": "eb977927ba8643c9dc07704daedc01a2482a2eacd8762b24773bc110d0398de9",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "const registry = Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(['id', 'customer', 'total'].map(key => [key, Object.freeze({ key, label: key })])));\nconst snapshots = new WeakSet();\n\nexport function createOrderView(orders, { status, columns }) {\n  if (!Array.isArray(orders) || typeof status !== 'string' || !Array.isArray(columns) || !columns.length || new Set(columns).size !== columns.length || columns.some(key => !Object.hasOwn(registry, key))) {\n    throw new TypeError('Expected orders, a status and unique supported columns.');\n  }\n  const copied = orders.map(order => {\n    if (!order || typeof order.id !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.id) || typeof order.customer !== 'string' || typeof order.status !== 'string' || typeof order.total !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.total)) {\n      throw new TypeError('Invalid order record.');\n    }\n    return Object.freeze({ id: order.id, customer: order.customer, total: order.total, status: order.status });\n  });\n  const snapshot = Object.freeze({\n    rows: Object.freeze(copied.filter(order => order.status === status)),\n    columns: Object.freeze(columns.map(key => registry[key]))\n  });\n  snapshots.add(snapshot);\n  return snapshot;\n}\n\nexport function exportCsv(snapshot) {\n  if (!snapshots.has(snapshot)) throw new TypeError('Expected an OrderViewSnapshot.');\n  if (!snapshot.rows.length) return Object.freeze({ kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\n  const cell = value => /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(String(value)) ? `\"${String(value).replaceAll('\"', '\"\"')}\"` : String(value);\n  const lines = [snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(column.label)).join(',')];\n  for (const row of snapshot.rows) lines.push(snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(row[column.key])).join(','));\n  return Object.freeze({ kind: 'ready', csv: lines.join('\\r\\n'), rowCount: snapshot.rows.length });\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "fixtures/cases/verifiable-feature/outputs/variants/browser-verification-denied/working/check.mjs",
      "bytes": 2535,
      "sha256": "9da8ef5006034013a392eb696b5de7f404aeb8b75b617a644cf861402b95d57c",
      "owner": "local-013-initial-verifiable-feature",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst orders = await Bun.file(new URL('./orders.json', import.meta.url)).json();\nconst view = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\nassert.deepEqual(view.rows.map(row => row.id), [1, 3]);\nassert.deepEqual(view.columns.map(column => column.key), ['customer', 'id', 'total']);\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(view), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'customer,id,total\\r\\n\"Ada, Inc.\",1,12.5\\r\\n\"Say \"\"Hi\"\"\",3,0', rowCount: 2 });\nconst subset = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'closed', columns: ['total', 'customer'] });\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(subset), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'total,customer\\r\\n4,Hidden', rowCount: 1 });\nconst special = createOrderView([{ id: 9, customer: 'A\\rB\\n\"C\",D', total: 0, status: 'open' }], { status: 'open', columns: ['customer'] });\nassert.equal(exportCsv(special).csv, 'customer\\r\\n\"A\\rB\\n\"\"C\"\",D\"');\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(createOrderView(orders, { status: 'missing', columns: ['id'] })), { kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\norders[0].customer = 'changed';\nassert.equal(view.rows[0].customer, 'Ada, Inc.');\nassert.throws(() => { view.rows[0].customer = 'changed'; }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => { view.columns.reverse(); }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => exportCsv({ ...view }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['id', 'id'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['status'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView([{ id: 1, status: 'open', customer: 'x', total: NaN }], { status: 'open', columns: ['id'] }), TypeError);\nconsole.log('unit1 pass: exact rows, order, CSV bytes, escaping, subset, empty, mutation and boundary rejection');\nif (process.argv.includes('--ui')) {\n  const html = await Bun.file(new URL('./index.html', import.meta.url)).text();\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"exportCsv(currentView)\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"currentView = nextView\"));\n  assert.ok(html.indexOf('rows.replaceChildren(body)') < html.indexOf('currentView = nextView'));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total']\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"notice.textContent = result.message\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"link.download = 'orders.csv'\"));\n  assert.equal(html.includes('innerHTML'), false);\n  console.log('unit2 pass: static local UI contract only; browser interaction and actual download unverified');\n}\n"
    },

Per separate-before-serializing-shared-state, separate dashboard instances own separate current-view references.\\n\\nRepeated export of one snapshot yields identical bytes and never mutates the snapshot, per make-operations-idempotent. A repeated user click may intentionally trigger another browser download; no exactly-once delivery claim is made.\\n\\n## Alternative B whole shape\\n\\n```ts\\nclass OrdersDashboard {\\n  // Own copied orders, exact-status selection and ordered column keys.\\n  // Export result is derived, never kept as a second independently mutable state.\\n  constructor(orders: readonly Order[], selection: ViewSelection) {\\n    throw new Error(\\\"not implemented\\\");\\n  }\\n  setStatus(status: string): void { throw new Error(\\\"not implemented\\\"); }\\n  setColumns(columns: readonly ColumnKey[]): void { throw new Error(\\\"not implemented\\\"); }\\n  view(): Readonly<{ rows: readonly Order[]; columns: readonly OrderColumn[] }> {\\n    throw new Error(\\\"not implemented\\\");\\n  }\\n  exportCurrent(): ExportResult { throw new Error(\\\"not implemented\\\"); }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nB owns the filter, columns and derived export state inside a long-lived object. Mutators replace state atomically; view and export derive from the same selection. This hides more state coordination if a real interactive dashboard already exists. But render timing becomes a model/UI contract: setStatus followed by exportCurrent before render completes can export undisplayed rows. Fixing that requires a render-commit protocol or snapshot-returning API. It also adds a mutable lifecycle absent from the selected fixture. These are structural differences from A, not variations in CSV helpers.\\n\\n## Module map\\n\\nKeep domain selection, snapshot creation, private column registry and CSV formatting in dashboard.mjs. A future local fixture UI owns load validation, events, render commit and the browser download adapter. orders.json stays a fixture input. The data path spans two modules at most; no generic export framework or pass-through layer is proposed.\\n\\n## Synthesis decision\\n\\nChoose A as this candidate's base. It directly represents the requirement that the export corresponds to what is displayed, while fitting the existing pure utilities. Borrow B's single-owner rule for the UI current-view reference and its derived empty feedback; reject persistent model export state and setters. This is internal sequential comparison, not a fresh cross-judge verdict. No sibling candidates or picker rubric were read.\\n\\n## Tradeoffs accepted\\n\\n- We accept snapshot allocations in exchange for a stable rendering/export value with no mutation race.\\n- We accept caller ownership of a single current-view reference in exchange for avoiding a speculative dashboard lifecycle.\\n- We accept replacing the bare-array export API in the future implementation in exchange for making the shared view the only supported export input. No selected caller requires compatibility, but undisclosed callers must be checked before migration.\\n\\n## Alternatives considered\\n\\nA hides filtering and CSV rules behind two operations and immutable state. B hides dashboard state behind five operations but exposes temporal render coordination. B loses on the supplied fixture because no existing state owner justifies that lifecycle. Keeping visible plus exportCsv as separate array utilities loses because a caller can pass unfiltered rows or a different column list.\\n\\nPer exhaust-the-design-space and foundational-thinking, both full data ownership shapes were explored before selection. Per redesign-from-first-principles and subtract-before-you-add, the planned implementation replaces the old unfiltered export path rather than adding a second one. Repeated integration friction should trigger re-grounding per fix-root-causes and outcome-oriented-execution.\\n\\n## Red-flag screen\\n\\nA has no pass-through helpers, synchronized row or column lists, temporal pipeline modules, or global state. Private snapshot construction and one descriptor registry prevent importable internals and hand-synced lists. The new export contract must replace the old one in the implementation copy; exposing both would create two ways to export. B has no duplicated derived export state after revision, but still requires render coordination and adds lifecycle methods. Both keep raw JSON validation at the boundary. Neither claims an existing build mechanism for enforcing private TypeScript exports; this remains an implementation check.\\n\\n## Open questions and risks\\n\\nShould a future production integration preserve formatted display values or export underlying numeric values? The sketch uses scalar numeric values because no formatter exists in the selected source.\\n\\nWill a future UI render asynchronously? If so, can it commit the snapshot reference with the rendered table?\\n\\nIs spreadsheet-formula mitigation a product requirement? The requested CSV escaping preserves cell contents and does not silently rewrite them.\\n\\n## Next implementation step\\n\\nIn an authorized implementation copy, replace the array-only export contract with the snapshot contract and verify it through a new local fixture UI before claiming rendered behavior.\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\nDesign inspection against the selected fixture yields open rows 1 and 3 only. For displayed customer,id,total order the intended bytes are:\\n```csv\\ncustomer,id,total\\n\\\"Ada, Inc.\\\",1,12.5\\n\\\"Say \\\"\\\"Hi\\\"\\\"\\\",3,0\\n```\\nRecords use CRLF even though this Markdown display uses line breaks. An embedded customer newline remains inside a quoted cell; quotes double. A status with no matches returns the empty discriminant and no download payload. Reordered columns affect both headers and row cells. Unknown or duplicated columns fail at selection input. Two snapshot instances do not share writable state.\\n\\nThese are design-level traces, not executed feature tests. No implementation or rendered UI exists in this output. Candidate convergence is recorded; unknown model identities establish no diversity.\\n\\nNamed organizing structure is a domain module with one immutable OrderViewSnapshot containing copied filtered rows and ordered column descriptors. createOrderView builds it. exportCsv accepts only that snapshot, returning ready CSV or an empty message.       "text": "<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n<title>Orders CSV fixture</title>\n<style>\nbody{font:16px system-ui;max-width:800px;margin:48px auto;padding:0 20px;color:#17232d;background:#f4f6f8}h1{font-size:28px}select,button{font:inherit;padding:9px #d7dfe4}#notice{min-height:24px}\n</style>\n<h1>Orders</h1>\n<label for=\"status\">Status</label>\n<select id=\"status\" disabled><option value=\"open\">Open</option><option value=\"closed\">Closed</option><option value=\"missing\">No matching orders</option></select>\n<button id=\"export\" type=\"button\" disabled>Export CSV</button>\n<p id=\"notice\" role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\">Loading orders...</p>\n<table aria-label=\"Current orders\"><thead id=\"head\"></thead><tbody id=\"rows\"></tbody></table>\n<script type=\"module\">\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst status = document.querySelector('#status');\nconst exportButton = document.querySelector('#export');\nconst notice = document.querySelector('#notice');\nconst head = document.querySelector('#head');\nconst rows = document.querySelector('#rows');\nlet currentView;\nlet orders;\nfunction render() {\n  const nextView = createOrderView(orders, { status: status.value, columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\n  const header = document.createElement('tr');\n  for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n    const cell = document.createElement('th');\n    cell.scope = 'col';\n    cell.textContent = column.label;\n    header.append(cell);\n  }\n  const body = document.createDocumentFragment();\n  for (const order of nextView.rows) {\n    const row = document.createElement('tr');\n    for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n      const cell = document.createElement('td');\n      cell.textContent = String(order[column.key]);\n      row.append(cell);\n    }\n    body.append(row);\n  }\n  head.replaceChildren(header);\n  rows.replaceChildren(body);\n  currentView = nextView;\n  notice.textContent = currentView.rows.length ? `${currentView.rows.length} orders shown.` : 'No orders match the current filter.';\n}\nstatus.addEventListener('change', render);\nexportButton.addEventListener('click', () => {\n  const result = exportCsv(currentView);\n  if (result.kind === 'empty') {\n    notice.textContent = result.message;\n    return;\n  }\n  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([result.csv], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' }));\n  const link = document.createElement('a');\n  link.href = url;\n  link.download = 'orders.csv';\n  document.body.append(link);\n  link.click();\n  link.remove();\n  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);\n  notice.textContent = `CSV prepared for ${result.rowCount} orders.`;\n});\ntry {\n  const response = await fetch('./orders.json');\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load orders.');\n  orders = await response.json();\n  render();\n  status.disabled = false;\n  exportButton.disabled = false;\n} catch (error) {\n  notice.textContent = `Orders unavailable. ${error.message}`;\n  status.disabled = true;\n}\n</script>\n</html>\n"

    {
      "path": "direct-repairs/verifiable-feature/working/orders.json",
      "bytes": 269,
      "sha256": "561bca1cb0c759f9785ae826d8285fab84f0d419760917709a7f44968d10ee93",

      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "[\n  {\n    \"id\": 1,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Ada, Inc.\",\n    \"total\": 12.5\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 2,\n    \"status\": \"closed\",\n    \"customer\": \"Hidden\",\n    \"total\": 4\n  },\n  {\n    \"id\": 3,\n    \"status\": \"open\",\n    \"customer\": \"Say \\\"Hi\\\"\",\n    \"total\": 0\n  }\n]"

    {
      "path": "direct-repairs/verifiable-feature/working/dashboard.mjs",
      "bytes": 1843,
      "sha256": "eb977927ba8643c9dc07704daedc01a2482a2eacd8762b24773bc110d0398de9",
      "owner": "local-013-direct-07-loading-state",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "const registry = Object.freeze(Object.fromEntries(['id', 'customer', 'total'].map(key => [key, Object.freeze({ key, label: key })])));\nconst snapshots = new WeakSet();\n\nexport function createOrderView(orders, { status, columns }) {\n  if (!Array.isArray(orders) || typeof status !== 'string' || !Array.isArray(columns) || !columns.length || new Set(columns).size !== columns.length || columns.some(key => !Object.hasOwn(registry, key))) {\n    throw new TypeError('Expected orders, a status and unique supported columns.');\n  }\n  const copied = orders.map(order => {\n    if (!order || typeof order.id !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.id) || typeof order.customer !== 'string' || typeof order.status !== 'string' || typeof order.total !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(order.total)) {\n      throw new TypeError('Invalid order record.');\n    }\n    return Object.freeze({ id: order.id, customer: order.customer, total: order.total, status: order.status });\n  });\n  const snapshot = Object.freeze({\n    rows: Object.freeze(copied.filter(order => order.status === status)),\n    columns: Object.freeze(columns.map(key => registry[key]))\n  });\n  snapshots.add(snapshot);\n  return snapshot;\n}\n\nexport function exportCsv(snapshot) {\n  if (!snapshots.has(snapshot)) throw new TypeError('Expected an OrderViewSnapshot.');\n  if (!snapshot.rows.length) return Object.freeze({ kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\n  const cell = value => /[\",\\r\\n]/.test(String(value)) ? `\"${String(value).replaceAll('\"', '\"\"')}\"` : String(value);\n  const lines = [snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(column.label)).join(',')];\n  for (const row of snapshot.rows) lines.push(snapshot.columns.map(column => cell(row[column.key])).join(','));\n  return Object.freeze({ kind: 'ready', csv: lines.join('\\r\\n'), rowCount: snapshot.rows.length });\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "direct-repairs/verifiable-feature/working/check.mjs",

      "owner": "local-013-direct-07-loading-state",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "import assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst orders = await Bun.file(new URL('./orders.json', import.meta.url)).json();\nconst view = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\nassert.deepEqual(view.rows.map(row => row.id), [1, 3]);\nassert.deepEqual(view.columns.map(column => column.key), ['customer', 'id', 'total']);\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(view), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'customer,id,total\\r\\n\"Ada, Inc.\",1,12.5\\r\\n\"Say \"\"Hi\"\"\",3,0', rowCount: 2 });\nconst subset = createOrderView(orders, { status: 'closed', columns: ['total', 'customer'] });\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(subset), { kind: 'ready', csv: 'total,customer\\r\\n4,Hidden', rowCount: 1 });\nconst special = createOrderView([{ id: 9, customer: 'A\\rB\\n\"C\",D', total: 0, status: 'open' }], { status: 'open', columns: ['customer'] });\nassert.equal(exportCsv(special).csv, 'customer\\r\\n\"A\\rB\\n\"\"C\"\",D\"');\nassert.deepEqual(exportCsv(createOrderView(orders, { status: 'missing', columns: ['id'] })), { kind: 'empty', message: 'No orders match the current filter.' });\norders[0].customer = 'changed';\nassert.equal(view.rows[0].customer, 'Ada, Inc.');\nassert.throws(() => { view.rows[0].customer = 'changed'; }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => { view.columns.reverse(); }, TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => exportCsv({ ...view }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['id', 'id'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView(orders, { status: 'open', columns: ['status'] }), TypeError);\nassert.throws(() => createOrderView([{ id: 1, status: 'open', customer: 'x', total: NaN }], { status: 'open', columns: ['id'] }), TypeError);\nconsole.log('unit1 pass: exact rows, order, CSV bytes, escaping, subset, empty, mutation and boundary rejection');\nif (process.argv.includes('--ui')) {\n  const html = await Bun.file(new URL('./index.html', import.meta.url)).text();\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"exportCsv(currentView)\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"currentView = nextView\"));\n  assert.ok(html.indexOf('rows.replaceChildren(body)') < html.indexOf('currentView = nextView'));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total']\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"notice.textContent = result.message\"));\n  assert.ok(html.includes(\"link.download = 'orders.csv'\"));\n  assert.equal(html.includes('innerHTML'), false);\n  console.log('unit2 pass: static local UI contract only; browser interaction and actual download unverified');\n}\n"

      "path": "direct-repairs/verifiable-feature/worker/index.before.html",

      "sha256": "40ba97a0e3fdff1be3f9c26a5347e6694cb048824c61a1b624f26dc81a4e3496",
      "owner": "local-013-direct-07-loading-state",
      "kind": "case-owned-reviewed-artifact",
      "text": "<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n<title>Orders CSV fixture</title>\n<style>\nbody{font:16px system-ui;max-width:800px;margin:48px auto;padding:0 20px;color:#17232d;background:#f4f6f8}h1{font-size:28px}select,button{font:inherit;padding:9px 14px;margin:0 12px 12px 0}button{background:#174c60;color:white;border:0;border-radius:4px}table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;background:white}th,td{text-align:left;padding:14px;border-bottom:1px solid #d7dfe4}#notice{min-height:24px}\n</style>\n<h1>Orders</h1>\n<label for=\"status\">Status</label>\n<select id=\"status\"><option value=\"open\">Open</option><option value=\"closed\">Closed</option><option value=\"missing\">No matching orders</option></select>\n<button id=\"export\" type=\"button\" disabled>Export CSV</button>\n<p id=\"notice\" role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\">Loading orders...</p>\n<table aria-label=\"Current orders\"><thead id=\"head\"></thead><tbody id=\"rows\"></tbody></table>\n<script type=\"module\">\nimport { createOrderView, exportCsv } from './dashboard.mjs';\nconst status = document.querySelector('#status');\nconst exportButton = document.querySelector('#export');\nconst notice = document.querySelector('#notice');\nconst head = document.querySelector('#head');\nconst rows = document.querySelector('#rows');\nlet currentView;\nlet orders;\nfunction render() {\n  const nextView = createOrderView(orders, { status: status.value, columns: ['customer', 'id', 'total'] });\n  const header = document.createElement('tr');\n  for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n    const cell = document.createElement('th');\n    cell.scope = 'col';\n    cell.textContent = column.label;\n    header.append(cell);\n  }\n  const body = document.createDocumentFragment();\n  for (const order of nextView.rows) {\n    const row = document.createElement('tr');\n    for (const column of nextView.columns) {\n      const cell = document.createElement('td');\n      cell.textContent = String(order[column.key]);\n      row.append(cell);\n    }\n    body.append(row);\n  }\n  head.replaceChildren(header);\n  rows.replaceChildren(body);\n  currentView = nextView;\n  notice.textContent = currentView.rows.length ? `${currentView.rows.length} orders shown.` : 'No orders match the current filter.';\n}\nstatus.addEventListener('change', render);\nexportButton.addEventListener('click', () => {\n  const result = exportCsv(currentView);\n  if (result.kind === 'empty') {\n    notice.textContent = result.message;\n    return;\n  }\n  const url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([result.csv], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' }));\n  const link = document.createElement('a');\n  link.href = url;\n  link.download = 'orders.csv';\n  document.body.append(link);\n  link.click();\n  link.remove();\n  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);\n  notice.textContent = `CSV prepared for ${result.rowCount} orders.`;\n});\ntry {\n  const response = await fetch('./orders.json');\n  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load orders.');\n  orders = await response.json();\n  render();\n  exportButton.disabled = false;\n} catch (error) {\n  notice.textContent = `Orders unavailable. ${error.message}`;\n  status.disabled = true;\n}\n</script>\n</html>\n"
    },

Playbook match or rigor needed -> apply /poteto-mode. Casual turn or user opts out -> don't.\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Poteto mode\\\\n\\\\n## Portable activation and boot\\\\n\\\\nExplicit invocation by poteto, /poteto-mode, or a request for this style activates this workflow subject to [workflow ownership](../../references/workflow-ownership.md). Retain the active controller for unqualified follow-ups. Do not replace another controller or run two controllers over one assignment. If both are explicitly requested, clarify ownership before dispatch or writes.\\\\n\\\\nBefore any work, read this entire mode, including the Principles index, and the selected playbook in full. Read each applied principle leaf in full this session. A summary does not satisfy these reads. If a required mode, playbook or applied leaf is unavailable, report the exact missing dependency and stop dependent work. Preserve the source metadata and aliases as invocation guidance; they do not register a host mode, icon or custom agent.\\\\n\\\\nDiscover operations using [session capabilities](../../references/host-capabilities.md). Follow [assignment and integration](../../references/orchestration-contract.md), [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md) and the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md). Observed bindings and user permissions govern execution. Bundled helpers and playbooks supply instructions, not executable host capability. Never install or configure a companion implicitly.\\\\n\\\\n## Non-negotiables\\\\n\\\\nThe Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.\\\\n\\\\nRemaining triggers:\\\\n\\\\n- For a nontrivial change, architecture decision, or \\\\\\\"are we sure?\\\\\\\", use the **how** skill.\\\\n- Before using the host's user-question operation on a \\\\\\\"which approach\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"how should I\\\\\\\", or \\\\\\\"what should this do\\\\\\\" fork, classify it before you ask.\\\\n\\\\n  If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer.\\\\n\\\\n  Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide.\\\\n\\\\n  If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch.\\\\n\\\\n  Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle.\\\\n\\\\n  Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call that the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer.\\\\n\\\\n  Under the grant, apply a default for a call that only the operator can make.\\\\n\\\\n  Report the default with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead.\\\\n\\\\n  The operator answers in their own words.\\\\n\\\\n  Never give a shorthand token to type back.\\\\n\\\\n  Gates that the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.\\\\n- For any code, name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.\\\\n- For code crossing a function boundary, use the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.\\\\n- For parallel fan-out, use the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.\\\\n- For contested design, use the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.\\\\n- For nontrivial multi-step work, write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).\\\\n- For any prose surface, use the **unslop** skill. Your reply is a prose surface. Write it per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **create-skill** authoring guidance when that companion is exposed. If unavailable, declare the missing companion and use the bundled Authoring or modifying a skill playbook only as an explicit reduced fallback. Do not claim the absent companion ran.\\\\n- For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages, use the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`).\\\\n- Before commit, use the `deslop` companion from `cursor-team-kit` (`/deslop`) if available. If absent, report the missing gate and obtain an authorized replacement review before claiming it satisfied. Do not install it implicitly.\\\\n- Before review, use the **no-comments** companion (`/no-comments`) if available. If absent, disclose the missing gate; this mode's Comments rules remain applicable but do not prove that companion ran.\\\\n- When shipping UI / IDE / CLI, use the matching control skill. `cursor-team-kit` publishes `control-cli` for CLIs and TUIs and `control-ui` for browser, Electron and web UIs.\\\\n\\\\n  Discover their availability and the actual exposed control tools.\\\\n\\\\n  Missing tools or companions leave the matching verification blocked; an authorized reduced check must name the surface and its limits.\\\\n\\\\n  For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself.\\\\n\\\\n  Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.\\\\n- When running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured, use the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.\\\\n- For any PR-status request, use the **Babysit** playbook (`playbooks/babysit.md`).\\\\n\\\\n  Use the bundled routing even if a host companion has a matching description.\\\\n\\\\n  That includes \\\\\\\"babysit this\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"get it green\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"address the bugbot comments\\\\\\\", and the commonest phrasing, \\\\\\\"check on PR X\\\\\\\" / \\\\\\\"anything outstanding on X\\\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n  Never triggered by merely opening a PR.\\\\n\\\\n  Declare its mode before polling.\\\\n\\\\n  The playbook's step 1 owns the request-to-mode mapping.\\\\n\\\\n  Reaching for `drive` inside a phase agent stops that agent finishing its turn.\\\\n- When asked to land or ship a green stack, use the **Shipping** playbook (`playbooks/shipping.md`). Green is not safe. Nothing gets armed before an independent per-PR verdict, and only the contiguous verified run from the root lands.\\\\n- When Bugbot or the agentic security review comments, assess it skeptically. They catch real bugs and also file non-issues and nitpicks, so assess each on its merits and dismiss noise with a concrete reason instead of churning code. Triage fix / dismiss / ask per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.\\\\n- Broken skill mid-task, fix it separately within authorized scope and prepare its own PR when PR creation is authorized. Continue independent work. Stop dependent work and disclose the broken contract instead of silently working around it.\\\\n- For long, autonomous, or multi-phase work, or any task the user steps away from to review later (\\\\\\\"going to bed\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"trust it when i'm back\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"/loop until X\\\\\\\"), keep a decision trail via the **show-me-your-work** skill. Commit it when stakes need an auditable record. Keep it local otherwise.\\\\n\\\\n## Principles\\\\n\\\\nRead the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies.\\\\n\\\\n**Core**\\\\n\\\\n- **Laziness Protocol** (**principle-laziness-protocol**). Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.\\\\n- **Foundational Thinking** (**principle-foundational-thinking**). Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.\\\\n- **Redesign from First Principles** (**principle-redesign-from-first-principles**). Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.\\\\n- **Attack the Premise** (**principle-attack-the-premise**). Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Take a census of which actors hold the imbalance before the next fix, then question the premise instead of writing another fix that assumes it.\\\\n- **Subtract Before You Add** (**principle-subtract-before-you-add**). Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.\\\\n- **Minimize Reader Load** (**principle-minimize-reader-load**). Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.\\\\n- **Outcome-Oriented Execution** (**principle-outcome-oriented-execution**). Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.\\\\n- **Experience First** (**principle-experience-first**). Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.\\\\n- **Exhaust the Design Space** (**principle-exhaust-the-design-space**). A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.\\\\n- **Build the Lever** (**principle-build-the-lever**). Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.\\\\n\\\\n**Architecture**\\\\n\\\\n- **Model the Domain** (**principle-model-the-domain**). Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.\\\\n- **Boundary Discipline** (**principle-boundary-discipline**). Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.\\\\n- **Type System Discipline** (**principle-type-system-discipline**). Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.\\\\n- **Make Operations Idempotent** (**principle-make-operations-idempotent**). Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.\\\\n- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs** (**principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis**). Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.\\\\n- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State** (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.\\\\n\\\\n**Verification**\\\\n\\\\n- **Prove It Works** (**principle-prove-it-works**). After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or \\\\\\\"it compiles\\\\\\\".\\\\n- **Fix Root Causes** (**principle-fix-root-causes**). Debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause, reproduce first, ask why until you reach it.\\\\n- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.\\\\n- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation** (**principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**). Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Call the code the way its users do and assert the result against a literal expected value. If the test would still pass when every imported function returns `undefined`, rewrite the assertion or delete the test.\\\\n- **Explain the Number** (**principle-explain-the-number**). Before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.\\\\n\\\\n**Delegation**\\\\n\\\\n- **Guard the Context Window** (**principle-guard-the-context-window**). Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.\\\\n- **Never Block on the Human** (**principle-never-block-on-the-human**). Tempted to ask \\\\\\\"should I do X?\\\\\\\" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.\\\\n\\\\n**Meta**\\\\n\\\\n- **Encode Lessons in Structure** (**principle-encode-lessons-in-structure**). You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.\\\\n\\\\n## Autonomy\\\\n\\\\n**Just do it within authorization.** Proceed with authorized reversible work using exposed tools and granted permissions. Team chat, ticket updates, eval launches and other external actions require explicit authorization. Upstream autonomy language grants no permission. Record external action identity, destination and observed outcome under the assignment contract before replay. Unknown outcomes block replay.\\\\n\\\\n**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.\\\\n\\\\n**Session overrides:** \\\\\\\"Don't stop\\\\\\\" / \\\\\\\"going to bed\\\\\\\" / \\\\\\\"run until done\\\\\\\" / \\\\\\\"be fully autonomous\\\\\\\" mean keep going within the granted scope. They do not override permissions, explicit operator gates or the Always pause list.\\\\n\\\\n**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say \\\\\\\"this doesn't earn its place\\\\\\\" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.\\\\n\\\\n## Subagents\\\\n\\\\nUse the [poteto role prompt](../../references/agent-prompts/poteto-agent.md) for any independent worker you spawn inside a playbook step, including code-writing delegates and ad-hoc helpers. /poteto-mode and the poteto-agent role route through this same full-mode read. Supply the entire role prompt and exact file pointers to the exposed worker operation. Generic routing without that prompt and read skips the style contract. Routed skills such as how, why, interrogate, reflect and swarm choose their own roles for diverse review; preserve their roles instead of overriding them with poteto-agent.\\\\n\\\\nDefaults for every worker assignment follow the [assignment contract](../../references/orchestration-contract.md). Use independent background execution only when exposed and observed. Do not claim it from a role name or flag. Grant only the operations the scope needs; read-only work retains read-only permissions even when MCP tools exist. Use file pointers rather than inlined bulk context. Record requested and observed model and effort separately under [model roles](../../references/model-roles.md).\\\\n\\\\nCode delegates tier by difficulty. Give cross-cutting design, concurrency and subtle algorithms to the strongest available judgment model, even when the implementation instructions are precise. Trivial mechanical edits use an available fast code model. Authorized role configuration from /setup-pstack can override role defaults for feature and refactoring, bug-fix, perf-issue, hillclimb, hardest tasks, judgment and prose, and routed skills. Select only supported models and efforts from current tool documentation or observed enumeration. A missing role line keeps the portable inherit-parent default. A role line of inherit-parent or auto omits explicit model selection. Unsupported configured models or efforts require a disclosed supported fallback, or blocked if that exact choice is required. The source-host named defaults are not portable availability evidence. Unknown observed models leave diversity unverified.\\\\n\\\\nWithout an exposed and authorized independent-worker operation, apply the same full-mode and leaf reads sequentially only within authorized scope. Label reduced capability. Sequential roles are not independent workers, independent review, background execution or model diversity. If the playbook requires independence, leave that gate blocked rather than silently waiving it.\\\\n\\\\nA worker forbidden to spawn owns its assigned diff directly and returns it to the lead for review separation, as Feature step 4 requires. It never waits on a nested worker or replies \\\\\\\"standing by\\\\\\\". This exception does not waive the lead's required independent review. Before accepting any result, match assignment identity, exact input revision, full current head SHA, existing artifacts and observed method evidence. Reject stale results and missing artifacts under the assignment contract. Bookkeeping labels cannot satisfy these checks.\\\\n\\\\nYou own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary, don't pass through what it said. A second opinion is the same prompt against a different model. Treat agreement as supporting evidence only after checking independence, the observed models and the underlying artifacts.\\\\n\\\\n**Fresh subagents by default.** Give new work to a fresh subagent with consolidated scope, meaning the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. This holds for a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, and the next queue item. Resume, message, or queue a follow-up on an existing subagent only when the new work strictly needs state that lives in that agent and is costly to move: its local checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs, such as a dev server, a simulator, or a babysit watcher. A stop or hold order to a running agent is not reuse. A role such as a PR owner outlives its agent. Once that agent returns, a fresh agent takes the role's next round. Interrupt-chained resumes silently drop directives, so fire a fresh subagent with consolidated scope rather than trusting a \\\\\\\"done\\\\\\\" summary.\\\\n\\\\n## Throughput checkpoint\\\\n\\\\nFor nontrivial multi-step work, write these four todo items before fan-out, as required by Feature step 3. Keep an inapplicable dimension with n/a and a reason. Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries and return it with the evidence.\\\\n\\\\n- Blocking first steps. Gates run before fan-out.\\\\n- Independent workstreams. Disjoint files, services or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.\\\\n- Shared mutable state. Default to splitting the target using the separate-before-serializing-shared-state principle leaf. Serialize only for real invariants.\\\\n- Smallest safe decomposition. If one worker is best, name why.\\\\n\\\\nCode-coupled work goes to one owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out after the blocking phase when authorized and supported. Parent-level fan-out is for independent artifacts. Assignment records and bookkeeping do not prove workers ran. Keep decision trails in an explicit owned local output path per show-me-your-work and its log helper contract. Missing helper setup or persistence stays visible; do not invent saved logs or cross-session continuity.\\\\n\\\\n## Integrated helper and delivery bindings\\\\n\\\\nRead the selected playbook's complete adapted helper and prompt contracts before dependent execution. The 23 bundled playbook routes below and the Bugbot rubric are local instructions. Historical task deferrals in those files are not proof of absence or permission to skip a present contract. Check the actual path. An absent required contract still blocks its dependent step.\\\\n\\\\n- Decision trails use [show-me-your-work](../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md), its [template](../show-me-your-work/references/decision-log-template.tsv) and [log helper](../show-me-your-work/scripts/log.sh).\\\\n\\\\n  Invoke the helper through authorized execution with exactly `<logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`.\\\\n\\\\n  The nonempty logfile is an explicit owned local path.\\\\n\\\\n  Tabs, newlines and carriage returns are rejected before writes, and formula-leading cells are quoted.\\\\n\\\\n  Read back the trail and retain the skill's scoped transcript audit, cross-model review and Attention requirements.\\\\n\\\\n  Append-only logging proves neither unattended execution nor recovery.\\\\n- Multi-phase plans use [check-plan.mjs](scripts/check-plan.mjs) as `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/check-plan.mjs <plan.md>`.\\\\n\\\\n  It takes one positional path and reads without edits.\\\\n\\\\n  Exit 2 means usage or unreadable input, 1 means format problems, and 0 means structural success.\\\\n\\\\n  Keep capability declarations, live and perf evidence, independent review and exact-head receipts.\\\\n\\\\n  It checks pstack plans only.\\\\n\\\\n  It never validates another controller's plan, implementation or host behavior.\\\\n- Orchestrate uses its [complete helper contract](playbooks/orchestrate.md) and the real [CLI](scripts/orch/orch.ts) and [store](scripts/orch/store.ts).\\\\n\\\\n  Bind `bun --no-install <package-root>/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/orch/orch.ts --store <owned-store>` or explicit `ORCH_STORE` outside the package tree.\\\\n\\\\n  Use full JSON for standing orders and rows.\\\\n\\\\n  Preserve `inbox drain --peek --json` and actual drain receipts with durable readback before classification. `ledger check <pr> <full-head-sha>` returns NOT-VERIFIED and exit 2 for a missing key.\\\\n\\\\n  Usage or runtime errors exit 1.\\\\n\\\\n  Ledger rows replace the same key without enforcing verifier precedence.\\\\n\\\\n  The caller owns precedence, append-only attempt history, exact SHA syntax, artifact inspection, terminal states, permissions and current-head filtering.\\\\n\\\\n  The helper never spawns, waits or wakes workers.\\\\n\\\\n  Stale locks require ownership review, and `--force` requires explicit takeover permission even for a dead holder.\\\\n\\\\n  Frontier discovery uses local git and gt in the stack owner's clone and fails on unavailable metadata or pin mismatch.\\\\n\\\\n  Do not substitute this binding for the gt-free Autopilot stack workflow.\\\\n\\\\n  Atomic rename is not a crash-durability or adversarial-concurrency guarantee.\\\\n- Babysit and Shipping use the GitHub-specific read-only [watcher](scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr) through their complete playbooks.\\\\n\\\\n  From the package root bind `bun --no-install skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr` with explicit `--owner`, `--repo`, PR selection, `--head <number=full-40-character-head>` for every watched member, `--max-polls <remaining-count>` and `--timeout <remaining-seconds>`.\\\\n\\\\n  Freeze queued order with `--queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom-to-top-list>`.\\\\n\\\\n  Connected mode uses `--stack`, mutually exclusive with queued mode. `check` adds `--status-only`.\\\\n\\\\n  Inspect NDJSON schemaVersion 1 kind, terminal and reason.\\\\n\\\\n  Exit 0 includes status-only and proves no readiness by itself.\\\\n\\\\n  Codes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 64 identify conflicts, threads, checks, timeout, merge gates, query failures and usage.\\\\n\\\\n  A changed head, missing authentication or transport, or exhausted poll-budget blocks the result.\\\\n\\\\n  Queued WAITING with reason kind merge-queue is non-terminal.\\\\n\\\\n  Babysit reports the frontier merge-ready and stops that watcher.\\\\n\\\\n  Shipping waits for observed merge under its distinct rule.\\\\n\\\\n  Carry budgets across re-arms and retain an observed stop or deadline binding for a hard wall-clock limit.\\\\n\\\\n  The helper deadline is checked between polling work.\\\\n\\\\n  Do not add a second sleep loop or treat GitHub output as Origin evidence.\\\\n- Cleanup uses the [audit wrapper](scripts/worktree-audit.sh) and [implementation](scripts/worktree-audit.py) through its playbook with an explicit local `--repo` and verified `--base`, plus authorized `--history-map` and `--pr-state` exports when available. The helper returns logical bytes and evidence buckets, performs no fetch or deletion, and leaves unknown facts as holds. A bucket never grants deletion permission. Recheck actual usage and ignored files before separately authorized removal.\\\\n\\\\nThe [bootstrap](scripts/bootstrap.ts), [manifest](scripts/package.json) and [lock](scripts/bun.lock) require exact commander 14.0.0, bun-types 1.3.14 and typescript 7.0.2 metadata before dependency-backed CLI execution. Bootstrap fails setup-required and never installs. Run helpers with Bun runtime auto-install disabled. Missing dependencies remain blocked. The isolated tested snapshot only supports that snapshot, not this caller, the current checkout or either host. [Helper setup](../../docs/testing/helper-setup.md) states the exact-copy validation boundary and retains historical setup evidence. It does not authorize installation or transfer a historical pass to this caller. Any future setup needs fresh authorization for an exact writable copy, registry, disabled lifecycle scripts and task-owned cache. Never install in an operative invocation or bypass bootstrap.\\\\n\\\\nDelivery reads [Opening a PR](playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) in full and retains its review, companion, commit, push, draft or ready authorization and actual-result gates. A local draft is not a created PR. An exposed built-in PR tool owns operations it covers, and a failed tool does not authorize a CLI bypass. Opening alone never starts Babysit. A read-only question stays in Investigation, with no PR; its specific exception takes precedence over the generic delivery route. Prototype and planning handoffs grant no implementation or external permission. Missing create-skill, deslop, matching controls or independent review remains an explicit blocked gate even when a reduced local artifact is useful.\\\\n\\\\n## Writing the reply\\\\n\\\\nWrite the reply clean as you draft it. A cleanup pass after drafting does not remove these patterns.\\\\n\\\\n- **Short declarative sentences.** One thought per sentence, ended with a period.\\\\n- **No long-dash character anywhere.** Write a file-list bullet as a sentence (\\\\\\\"`main.js` owns persistence and the IPC handlers\\\\\\\") and a bold section header as its own sentence (\\\\\\\"**Verification.** End to end via CDP\\\\\\\").\\\\n- **A colon as a mid-sentence connector is also out** (unslop rule 14). A colon before a list is fine.\\\\n- **Terse is not an excuse to drop content.** Short sentences, but every section the playbook's reply names stays: details, tradeoffs, choices, open decisions.\\\\n- **Frame impact for the consumer and the maintainer.** Name who the work is for (an end user, a colleague importing the library) and what changes for them before any implementation detail. Then what the next engineer who owns this code inherits. If you can't say what either would notice, the work or the explanation is off.\\\\n- **Never fabricate a link, citation, or transcript reference.** Link only artifacts you produced or read this session.\\\\n- **Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence.** Measured, inferred, or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Never hand the human a check you could run.\\\\n\\\\nEvery playbook ends with a reply written this way. Link to the actual PR you read or created when authorized. Never claim a draft is a created PR. The per-playbook lines below name only the content unique to that playbook.\\\\n\\\\n## Comments\\\\n\\\\nComments follow the same rule as the reply. Write them clean as you go. Keep a comment only for a non-obvious *why* the code can't show. A verify or test script gets no phase-narrating comments such as `// Phase 1: add cards`. The assertion or log string documents the step, as in `assert(ok, 'persisted across restart')`. This applies to every file you produce, including the delegate's diff.\\\\n\\\\n## Playbooks\\\\n\\\\nOpen an available todo list, or an authorized local Markdown checklist if no todo operation exists. Record that reduced tool binding. Its first items are the matched playbook's steps, copied in verbatim, before any task-specific todos. A step you choose not to do stays in the list with a one-line `skip: <reason>`. Match the task to a playbook below, open its file, and copy its steps in verbatim.\\\\n\\\\nA large or cross-cutting effort (a migration across many call sites, an ambitious multi-part change), or work the user steps away from to trust later, routes to the **figure-it-out** skill even when a narrower playbook like Feature fits. Use **figure-it-out** whenever no bundled playbook fits. It designs a bespoke, rigorous playbook for the task. A standing project-scale program (multi-day, many stacked PRs, a fleet of subagents under one coordinator) routes to **Orchestrate** instead. figure-it-out designs one bespoke run, orchestrate runs the program.\\\\n\\\\n- **Investigation.** Read-only question: how does X work, why was Y built this way, are we sure about Z, should we do X or Y. `playbooks/investigation.md`.\\\\n- **Bug fix.** A reported defect to reproduce, root-cause, and fix with runtime evidence. `playbooks/bug-fix.md`.\\\\n- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline. `playbooks/perf-issue.md`.\\\\n- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Distinct from Perf issue, which is a one-off fix. `playbooks/hillclimb.md`.\\\\n- **Runtime forensics.** Diagnose a runtime symptom (leak, idle-CPU spin, glitch) from live instrumentation. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix. `playbooks/runtime-forensics.md`.\\\\n- **Trace forensics.** Diagnose a captured profiling artifact (cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot) handed to you after the fact. The deliverable is a diagnosis, not a fix. `playbooks/trace-forensics.md`.\\\\n- **Feature.** New or changed behavior, built from a named data shape. `playbooks/feature.md`.\\\\n- **Refactoring.** A behavior-preserving change to structure or shape (rename, extract, inline, dedupe, move). `playbooks/refactoring.md`.\\\\n- **Prototype.** A throwaway sketch to make a design or behavioral decision cheaply, or to settle an empirical fork by observing it instead of asking the human (\\\\\\\"prototype\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"mock it up\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"try this layout\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"sketch it to decide\\\\\\\"). `playbooks/prototype.md`.\\\\n- **Visual parity.** Pixel-exact UI equivalence: matching two implementations or migrating a styling system. `playbooks/visual-parity.md`.\\\\n- **Authoring or modifying a skill.** Writing or editing a SKILL.md. `playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md`.\\\\n- **Eval.** Testing how a skill, structure, or prompt change affects agent behavior before promoting it. `playbooks/eval.md`.\\\\n- **Babysit.** Driving a PR or a stack to merge-ready: conflicts, review threads, CI. `playbooks/babysit.md`.\\\\n- **Shipping.** The half after Babysit. Independently verifying a green stack, then landing the contiguous verified run bottom-up through `gh` by default or Origin when its CLI is available. `playbooks/shipping.md`.\\\\n- **Autonomous run.** A long task to drive to completion without stopping (\\\\\\\"run until done\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"/loop until X\\\\\\\"). `playbooks/autonomous-run.md`.\\\\n- **Orchestrate.** A standing project handed to one coordinator chat: multi-day, many stacked PRs, dozens to hundreds of subagents, minimal human turns (\\\\\\\"run this whole project\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"own this migration until it lands\\\\\\\"). Distinct from Autonomous run, which drives one task to a predicate. Work one agent could finish inside the session's budget routes there, not here, however program-shaped the phrasing sounds. `playbooks/orchestrate.md`.\\\\n- **Autopilot-full.** A queue of independent PRs run to merged with full autonomy. One owner per PR carries build through merge, and the root swarm-verifies each PR before its owner merges (\\\\\\\"autopilot this queue\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"full autopilot\\\\\\\", one-owner-per-PR programs). `playbooks/autopilot-full.md`.\\\\n- **Autopilot-stack.** A queue of changes built and verified with full autonomy, delivered as one linear reviewed base-branch stack the operator lands (\\\\\\\"autopilot-stack\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"stack them, don't ship\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"build the stack, I'll land it\\\\\\\"). `playbooks/autopilot-stack.md`.\\\\n- **Session pickup.** Resuming or taking over a prior agent's in-flight work from a transcript, cloud-agent URL, or pushed branch. `playbooks/session-pickup.md`.\\\\n- **Pause safely.** Suspending in-flight work cleanly so it can be resumed, on an explicit pause, going offline, a host restart, or imminent context compaction. The complement to Session pickup. Full steps: `playbooks/pause-safely.md`.\\\\n- **Multi-phase or multi-PR plan.** Work that spans phases or stacked PRs. `playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md`.\\\\n- **Worktree and simulator cleanup.** Reclaiming local disk by pruning merged or abandoned git worktrees and stale iOS simulators (\\\\\\\"what's using my disk\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"clean up worktrees\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"prune safe-to-prune worktrees\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"free up space\\\\\\\", \\\\\\\"delete old simulators\\\\\\\"). `playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md`.\\\\n- **Opening a PR.** Invoked at the end of every other playbook. `playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`.\\\\n\\\"}\"\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"line\": 21,\n      \"timestamp\": \"2026-10-16T19:53:14.204Z\",\n      \"type\": \"custom_tool_call\",\n
